items.title: Lookman ruled out of Tanzania return leg with knee ligament sprain
items.description: Super Eagles forward Ademola Lookman has been ruled out of Nigeria’s 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying return-leg fixture against Tanzania following a knee ligament sprain. Promise Efoghe, Super Eagles Media Officer, confirmed the development to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Saturday. “Scan has revealed Ademola Lookman suffered a sprain in his knee ligament during yesterday’s match. “This rules him out of Nigeria’s next AFCON qualifier against Tanzania in Zanzibar on Tuesday,” Efoghe said. The injury was sustained during Nigeria’s 3-1 victory over Tanzania in their Matchday Three encounter at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo, on Friday. Lookman’s absence will be a setback for the Super Eagles as they prepare for the return fixture against the Taifa Stars. The Athletico Madrid forward has been an important attacking option for Nigeria, providing creativity, pace and goal-scoring threat in the final third. NAN reports that Friday’s victory strengthened Nigeria’s position in the qualifying campaign, taking their points tally to six. The Super Eagles will now travel to Zanzibar for Tuesday’s Matchday Four encounter, hoping to consolidate their position in the group. Nigeria will be seeking another positive result against Tanzania as the race for qualification for the 2027 AFCON finals gathers momentum. Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda are already guaranteed places at the tournament as co-hosts, leaving the remaining qualification spots to be contested by other countries. The 2027 AFCON finals will be jointly hosted by the three East African countries. (NAN) The post Lookman ruled out of Tanzania return leg with knee ligament sprain appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: CAN de beach soccer 2026 : le Maroc connaît son calendrier au Sénégal
items.description: La Confédération africaine de football (CAF) a dévoilé le calendrier de la CAN de beach soccer 2026, prévue du 28 novembre au 6 décembre à Saly, au Sénégal. Le Maroc, placé dans le groupe B avec la Mauritanie, le Malawi et l’Angola, débutera la compétition le 29 novembre face au Malawi. Le coup d’envoi de la compétition sera donné le samedi 28 novembre avec une première affiche entre le Mozambique et l’Ouganda, à 15h00 GMT. Le Sénégal, pays hôte et tenant du titre, fera ensuite son entrée en lice face au Ghana à 16h30 GMT. Le Maroc disputera son premier match le dimanche 29 novembre à 16h30 GMT, face au Malawi. Cette rencontre sera précédée du duel entre la Mauritanie, finaliste de la précédente édition, et l’Angola, programmé à 15h00 GMT. Le groupe B réunit donc la Mauritanie, le Maroc, le Malawi et l’Angola, tandis que le groupe A est composé du Sénégal, du Mozambique, de l’Ouganda et du Ghana. Chaque sélection disputera trois rencontres durant la phase de groupes, qui s’achèvera le 2 décembre. Les deux premières équipes de chaque poule accéderont aux demi-finales, programmées le 4 décembre. Le match pour la troisième place ainsi que la finale auront lieu le 6 décembre, au terme de neuf jours de compétition. La CAN de beach soccer 2026 revêt également un enjeu mondial puisque les deux finalistes décrocheront leur qualification pour la Coupe du monde de beach soccer de la FIFA 2027. Le Sénégal, sacré lors des cinq dernières éditions en 2016, 2018, 2021, 2022 et 2024, tentera de conserver son titre devant son public. La Mauritanie, finaliste en 2024, figure également parmi les prétendants au sacre. Le Maroc cherchera, pour sa part, à tirer son épingle du jeu dans un groupe où l’Angola disputera sa première phase finale de CAN de beach soccer. Initialement prévue du 7 au 15 novembre, la compétition a été reportée afin de tenir compte du calendrier des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026, organisés du 31 octobre au 13 novembre. items.title: Soludo demands reopening of Anambra court of appeal
items.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has called for the immediate reopening of the Court of Appeal in the state, arguing that the volume of litigation generated by Anambra, which he said is second only to Lagos, justifies its continued operation. Soludo made the demand during a church service marking the commencement of the 2026/2027 Legal Year of the Anambra State Judiciary. He also urged the Nigerian legal profession to abandon imported wigs and gowns in favour of locally produced alternatives, saying the continued importation of legal attire amounts to exporting employment opportunities that could be created in Nigeria. The special service was presided over by the Bishop of Aguata, Supervising Bishop of the Diocese of Awka and Coordinating Bishop of the Province on the Niger, Rt. Rev. Samuel Ezeofor. It was attended by judicial officers, legal practitioners and government functionaries. Addressing the gathering, Soludo reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to improving justice delivery but expressed concern over the continued closure of the Court of Appeal in Anambra. “Anambra, after Lagos, generates more cases. We are more deserving to have the Court of Appeal. “The Court of Appeal in Anambra should not be closed for one day if merit and need happen to be the criteria. Come and open your court,” he said. The governor also reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to the welfare of judicial officers and the provision of necessary infrastructure for the judiciary. He noted that the state’s plea-bargaining initiative was helping to decongest correctional facilities. On the need to promote local industries, Soludo challenged lawyers and judicial officers to embrace Nigerian-made legal attire rather than continue importing wigs and gowns. “Can we change the law regalia into what is made in Nigeria? We are creating jobs abroad by importing all the regalia you wear. “Let us eat what we produce and wear what we make. That is the way to help the economy. I wear Akwete to promote Made-in-Nigeria,” he said. The governor, who is known for wearing Akwete fabric, said adopting locally produced materials would support domestic industries and create employment opportunities. On security, Soludo highlighted the cooperation among the executive, legislature and judiciary, crediting the state’s Homeland Security Law with strengthening the security architecture and restoring calm in different parts of Anambra. “We may have different branches of government, but we have one objective: the security and welfare of Ndi Anambra,” he said. Addressing the crisis within the Awka Diocese of the Anglican Communion, the governor said his administration had maintained neutrality, describing the dispute as a private affair of the Anglican Church in Anambra and Nigeria. He, however, called for an amicable resolution, stressing that the government’s responsibility was to maintain law and order. In his remarks, the Chief Judge of Anambra State, Justice Onochie Anyachebelu, described the Legal Year ceremony as an opportunity for the judiciary to assess its performance and reposition itself for improved service delivery. While commending Soludo for maintaining a cordial working relationship with the judiciary, Anyachebelu appealed for urgent government intervention in areas requiring attention. “The Anambra State Judiciary needs help. Your presence has given us renewed hope,” the Chief Judge said. The post Soludo demands reopening of Anambra court of appeal appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Don’t disappoint Nigeria’s founding fathers, Jonathan warns political leaders
items.description: Former President Goodluck Jonathan has called on Nigeria’s political leaders to rebuild the country, warning against disappointing the founding fathers. This ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‌⁠​‌‍​‌‌​is contained in a statement issued by the former president’s Media Adviser, Mr Ikechukwu Eze, in Abuja on Saturday. Eze quoted Jonathan as making the call while delivering his address at a colloquium organised in honour of the 162nd birth anniversary of a nationalist, Pa Herbert Macaulay, at Nigerian Institute of International Affairs (NIIA), Lagos on Saturday. Jonathan, who was the chairman of the occasion, challenged Nigeria’s political leaders and citizens to reflect on whether the country had lived up to the dreams and aspirations of its founding nationalists. He asked whether Herbert Macaulay, Nnamdi Azikiwe, Obafemi Awolowo, Ahmadu Bello and other heroes of the independence struggle would be proud of today’s Nigeria or regret the outcome of their sacrifices. Speaking on the theme “Nationalism and Nation Building”, the former president said the vision of Nigeria’s founding nationalists went beyond the transfer of political power from colonial authorities to Nigerians. “They envisaged a sovereign, united and prosperous country where citizens would enjoy equal rights, economic opportunities, quality education, accessible healthcare and the benefits of accountable governance,” he said. Jonathan appealed that Nigeria must not allow its founding nationalists to regret the struggle they waged for independence. According to him, the greatest tribute to the nation’s heroes is not merely to celebrate their birthdays or preserve their monuments but to build a country that reflects the ideals for which they sacrificed. “We must not make Herbert Macaulay, Nnamdi Azikiwe, Obafemi Awolowo, Ahmadu Bello and the other founding nationalists regret, even in their graves, the struggle they waged for our independence,” he said. Jonathan urged the present generation to ensure that today’s national challenges were not allowed to become the inheritance of their children and grandchildren. He expressed concern that 66 years after independence, Nigeria had yet to substantially realise many of these aspirations. According to him, while Nigeria has recorded progress in several areas, patriotism demands the courage to confront its shortcomings, including leadership failures, institutional weaknesses, corruption, policy inconsistency, inadequate infrastructure, insecurity and over-dependence on raw material exports. Jonathan challenged Nigeria to learn from countries such as South Korea, India and Singapore, which had made remarkable advancement in industrialisation, technology, education, healthcare and human development. He noted that Nigeria’s enormous human and natural resources should have translated into comparable levels of development, questioning the obstacles that had continued to constrain the country’s potential. Distinguishing between independence and nation-building, Jonathan said that while winning independence was a historic achievement, building a prosperous, united and developed country remained an unfinished national responsibility. Looking ahead to Nigeria’s centenary of independence in 2060, he urged the present generation to begin asking what kind of country it intended to bequeath to future generations. He said the next 34 years must be used to establish measurable national development targets, strengthen institutions and build a productive economy capable of creating opportunities for young Nigerians. The former president also called for renewed commitment to Pan-Africanism, stressing that political independence must be complemented by economic emancipation, technological advancement, educational development and stronger continental integration. He particularly urged young Nigerians to see themselves as inheritors of the nationalist struggle, noting that the responsibility of advancing the ideals of freedom now rested on their shoulders through innovation, enterprise, civic participation and responsible citizenship. Outlining four critical areas requiring urgent attention, Jonathan called for comprehensive democratic reforms to strengthen popular participation, the rule of law, judicial independence, human rights and accountability. He also advocated reforms in political recruitment, insisting that competence, capacity and merit must take precedence over ethnic, religious and regional considerations in the selection of political leaders. On education, he called for a functional system that would prioritise technological advancement, innovation and knowledge production, adding that Nigerian universities must aspire to compete among the world’s leading institutions rather than remaining largely centres of knowledge consumption. He further emphasised the need to build strong, credible and independent institutions, stressing that sustainable national development would depend on strong institutions rather than the influence of individual leaders. Recalling the controversy surrounding Nigeria’s 2014 centenary celebrations, Jonathan said he had supported the commemoration in spite of criticisms from those who believed the country had not achieved sufficient progress to justify celebrating its 100 years of amalgamation. He explained that the importance of remembering history lies in understanding the nation’s journey, assessing its present condition and drawing lessons for a better future. The former president urged the organisers of the colloquium to move beyond historical reflections and generate concrete recommendations for repositioning Nigeria ahead of its 100th independence anniversary. ( NAN ) The post Don’t disappoint Nigeria’s founding fathers, Jonathan warns political leaders appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Internet Society of Ghana President urges Ghanaians to be responsible online, warns against social media overuse
items.description: President of the Internet Society of Ghana, Dr Maud Adjeley Ashong Elliot, has urged Ghanaians to adopt responsible online behaviour, warning that careless use of social media can affect their privacy, reputation, productivity and relationships. She said the internet had become an essential part of everyday life, making it important for both young and older people to understand how to navigate digital platforms safely. “The internet has come to stay, whether we like it or not. We have to make sure we adapt, and then we survive,” she said. Dr Ashong Elliot said this at the maiden public lecture of the Society of Private Medical and Dental Practitioners, held at the British Council on Friday, November 13, under the theme, “ Growing up online: Social media, mental health, and the future of Ghana’s youth .” She likened responsible online behaviour to the etiquette people are taught in their everyday lives, saying the growing use of digital platforms required users to be mindful of how they communicate and what they share. She cautioned that content posted online could remain accessible even after users attempted to delete it, as others might have saved or shared copies. “Whatever you put out there cannot be erased,” she said, urging users to pause and think carefully before posting or forwarding content. Dr Ashong Elliot also challenged users to pay closer attention to the terms and conditions of digital platforms, particularly WhatsApp, and not assume that end-to-end encryption offered complete protection. She said excessive phone use was also affecting people’s productivity, including in professional and learning environments. Sharing her personal experience, she said she had realised she was becoming too dependent on her phone and had introduced a schedule to check WhatsApp messages at intervals rather than constantly reaching for the device. She encouraged users to set boundaries around their screen time and protect their sleep by avoiding the habit of using their phones just before going to bed. On digital footprints, Dr Ashong Elliot urged people to search for their names online and take deliberate steps to shape the information available about them. She said individuals should be strategic about their online presence and pay attention to what is published about them, given how difficult it can be to correct or remove information once it circulates. She further advised users to be cautious about privacy settings, permissions granted to applications, and the personal information they share with online platforms. She also encouraged people to cover their computer webcams when they were not in use. Parents, she said, must take an active interest in their children’s online activities by checking the content they access on platforms such as YouTube. Dr Ashong Elliot also warned against the spread of misinformation, scams and phishing attempts, urging users to verify information before sharing it and to independently confirm requests for personal details. She said that people who forward harmful or inappropriate content also bear responsibility for its circulation, even if they did not create it. On artificial intelligence, she acknowledged its growing importance but urged users to engage with the technology ethically and pay attention to the privacy implications of the applications they use. “AI has also come. Please, it has come to stay, whether we like it or not. But what we want to preach is that let’s use it ethically,” she said. Also speaking at the event, UNICEF Ghana Child Protection Specialist Hilda Mensah warned that young people faced risks such as online grooming, cyberbullying and sextortion, which could have serious consequences for their mental health. She said such experiences could lead to depression, suicidal attempts, social isolation, strained relationships and a loss of trust in others. While acknowledging the benefits of the internet for learning, communication, business and skills development, she urged young people to use digital platforms in ways that support their personal growth and contribute positively to society. “Use the internet for your own development, innovation, learning, connecting positively, and making importantly a contribution to building your society, your community, your family, and yourself,” she said. Ms Mensah also cautioned young people against cyberbullying, hateful comments, and sharing content intended to embarrass or harm others. She reminded them that their online activities could have consequences beyond the present, urging them to think critically about what they post and how it might affect their future. “The internet never forgets,” she said, encouraging young people to build a positive digital footprint. Chairperson for the event, Evelyn Agyapong, called on young people to use the internet responsibly and take advantage of its benefits while avoiding activities that could negatively affect their mental health and future. She acknowledged that the internet had created opportunities for learning, communication, business, innovation and skills development, but said users must also be conscious of the risks associated with social media and other digital platforms. She noted that online grooming, cyberbullying and sextortion could have serious consequences for young people’s mental health, potentially leading to depression, suicidal attempts, social isolation, strained relationships and a loss of trust in others. Ms Agyapong urged young people to focus on the positive opportunities offered by the internet and avoid using digital platforms to bully others, make hateful comments or share content intended to ridicule or embarrass people. She said that responsible online behaviour was particularly important because digital activities could affect individuals long after content had been posted. “The internet never forgets,” she said, urging young people to build positive digital footprints that would not undermine their future opportunities.

items.title: Thousands rally in Antalya to demand climate justice as COP31 talks hit midpoint
items.description: Thousands of protesters on Saturday took to the streets in the Turkish city hosting COP31 to accuse the climate summit of failing those bearing the brunt of environmental destruction. The show of dissent comes as negotiators approach the crunch final week of global climate talks in Antalya, with nearly 200 nations scrambling to strike a deal by Friday. The summit is not expected to produce a major breakthrough, frustrating activists demanding tougher curbs on planet-warming fossil fuels and fresh pledges to help poorer countries adapt to climate impacts. In downtown Antalya, under rainy skies, thousands of protesters dressed in costumes and shouting slogans marched under close police supervision in the largest demonstration since COP31 began on Monday. “We are suffering the consequences of climate injustice, yet our voices are never heard at the COP,” said Halime Saman from the People’s Climate Summit platform, one of the groups behind the rally. “Turkiye is the co-chair of COP31 but still has no roadmap for phasing out fossil fuels. New power stations and coal mines are being opened,” she told AFP . Yasar Gokoglu, a 78-year-old demonstrator, travelled nearly 600 kilometres from Adana in southern Turkiye to denounce what he called “a masquerade sponsored by monopolies”. Protesters hold bird effigies during a demonstration organised by climate activists on the sidelines of the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya on Nov 14, 2026. — AFP Police estimated that more than 7,000 people attended the protest, which was organised by environmental groups, trade unions and rights organisations, and proceeded without any major incident. Civil society activists had raised safety concerns ahead of COP31 after Turkiye embarked on a crackdown on the LGBT community in September. Some LGBT protesters waving rainbow flags participated in the march. Demonstrators were only allowed to join the rally after being searched by police. ‘No quick fix’ Much smaller demonstrations inside the COP31 venue this week, including one attended by Swedish activist Greta Thunberg, have been mounting pressure on political leaders to act faster on the climate crisis. The negotiations hit the halfway point Saturday, but countries remain far apart on contentious issues including financing adaptation measures in developing nations, defending climate science, and shifting from fossil fuels to clean energy. Australia’s climate minister, Chris Bowen, who is chairing the formal negotiations, said there had been “really good and positive conversations” but some issues required more time. Outside the negotiations, Turkiye is urging countries to join a voluntary pledge to raise the share of global final energy demand met by electricity. The summit, which closes on Nov 20, takes place against a difficult backdrop, with a conflict-driven energy crisis and geopolitical tensions tempering expectations. “There’s no climate quick fix. No single COP can magic this crisis away, but each must drive progress,” UN climate chief Simon Stiell told reporters on Saturday. MNA presents five parliamentary recommendations At the Pakistan Pavilion at COP31, Parliamentary Secretary for Information and Broadcasting Barrister Danyal Chaudhry addressed a high-level dialogue and stressed that the world needs to acknowledge the economic cost of climate inaction, according to a press release . At the dialogue, titled ‘Adapting Under Austerity: Delivering Paris Commitments in Debt-Stressed, Climate-Vulnerable Economies’, he stated that Pakistan’s core needs to ensure that the pursuit of fiscal sustainability does not compromise Islamabad’s capacity to protect people from severe climate impacts. “He noted that past policies introduced in the name of fiscal consolidation increased taxation and discouraged climate-resilient development — an approach the Government of Pakistan believes directly undermined its climate objectives,” the press release said. Chaudhry emphasised that the world must “function as one global village and one global family”. The secretary further noted that addressing the climate crisis requires collective action on a shared planet and there cannot be separate standards for wealthy and developing nations. He presented five key parliamentary recommendations for climate-vulnerable and debt-stressed nations. “First, he called for climate-proofing fiscal and taxation policies by mandating climate impact assessments for major financial decisions so they do not drive up the cost of sustainable development,” the statement said. Second, he stressed the need to safeguard the transition to renewable energy through stable, predictable policies that do not penalise households or businesses investing in clean energy. Chaudhry also called on governments and lenders to treat adaptation as an investment rather than an expense, stressing that investing in climate-resilient agriculture, water management, early warning systems, and disaster-resistant infrastructure reduces future recovery costs. Next, he advocated for reforming global debt architecture through debt-for-climate swaps, climate-contingent clauses, concessional financing and extended repayment schedules, so disaster-prone countries are not forced to “sacrifice essential development”. Chaudhry went on to call for strengthening parliamentary oversight of climate financing by requiring annual reports on climate-related taxes, subsidies, budget allocations and measurable adaptation outcomes, the press release said. He added that national fiscal frameworks must remain fully aligned with Pakistan’s Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) and National Adaptation Plan.

items.title: Nigerian Mission hits back at Magwenya, insists Ramaphosa intervened
items.description: The Nigerian High Commission in South Africa has renewed its defence of newly accredited High Commissioner, Chief Femi Fani-Kayode, insisting that President Cyril Ramaphosa personally intervened in the controversy surrounding the presentation of his diplomatic credentials. The mission was responding to South African Presidency spokesperson, Vincent Magwenya, who accused Fani-Kayode of lying about Ramaphosa’s intervention following a disagreement over the omission of his address during Friday’s credentials presentation ceremony in Tshwane. In a strongly worded statement posted on X, the Nigerian High Commission accused Magwenya of making provocative and undiplomatic remarks, warning that his comments could undermine diplomatic relations between both countries. The commission said Magwenya had accused Fani-Kayode of lying and disgracing Nigeria barely hours after the envoy presented his letters of credence to the South African President. “You are the disgrace and no-one else. Outside of that your insolence and ignorance knows no bounds. You are bringing your nation into disrepute and wilfully and purposely burning the bridge of peace and reconciliation. That is a matter of concern to us,” the mission said. The controversy followed the apparent disruption of the South African Presidency’s YouTube livestream around the time Fani-Kayode was due to present his letters of credence to Ramaphosa. The broadcast subsequently resumed when the South African President was addressing the ambassadors. Fani-Kayode, who was the last diplomat to present his credentials, had expressed displeasure over the omission of his address from the ceremony. He said he subsequently spoke with Ramaphosa, who apologised and assured him that everything was fine. However, Magwenya disputed the Nigerian envoy’s account, prompting the Nigerian mission to insist that the South African President intervened to resolve the disagreement. The commission also recalled an earlier controversy in which Magwenya reportedly described concerns expressed by President Bola Tinubu and Ghanaian President John Mahama over xenophobia and Afrophobia in South Africa as fake news. It said Nigeria had ignored the earlier remarks but questioned why Magwenya would publicly describe its newly accredited envoy as a liar. “Did you really expect him to simply stomach your ill manners and keep quiet? If so you have misunderstood the character and nature of the Nigerian. We cannot be easily cowed,” the statement added. The mission further disclosed that several people, including newly accredited ambassadors from other countries, witnessed the proceedings and expressed displeasure over what transpired. It also claimed to possess a full video recording of the proceedings after the official photographs were taken, adding that it could release the footage if authorised to do so. Defending Ramaphosa’s handling of the disagreement, the commission said the South African President personally stepped in to resolve the matter and directed the relevant officials and state broadcaster to address the situation. “Thankfully your President had the decency and presence of mind to put out the fire and direct you and your state broadcaster to do the right thing. He literally saved the day,” it said. The Nigerian High Commission urged Magwenya to exercise restraint and allow diplomatic channels to resolve the disagreement, stressing that Nigeria remained interested in preserving cordial relations between both countries. It, however, warned against further escalation of the controversy. “To us this matter is closed but if you wish to escalate it you are welcome to do so and we are up to the task. A word is enough for the wise,” the commission declared. The post Nigerian Mission hits back at Magwenya, insists Ramaphosa intervened appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Netanyahu says only unity government can guarantee Israel’s security
items.description: Israel’s caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday reiterated his calls for a national unity government with his opponent Gadi Eisenkot, as well as his vow to eliminate the threat from Iran. A meeting with Eisenkot on Thursday “only strengthened the conviction that it is essential to form a national unity government” to guarantee Israel’s security, Netanyahu said in a video statement, adding that such a government could “eliminate the Iranian threat once and for all”. He said this government would be made up of parties that recognise Israel “as a state for the Jewish people”. It would address security challenges, he added, most notably Iran which he claimed would “not hesitate to use nuclear weapons against us”. With backing from 67 lawmakers following last month’s election, Eisenkot was tapped on Sunday to form a new government within 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension. Negotiations are expected to be difficult, especially as Netanyahu has waged a campaign to discredit Arab-Israeli parties, which gained a record number of seats in the election. Netanyahu’s proposed unity government would be made up of key Jewish parties ranging from the centre to the right, while excluding the Arab parties. Eisenkot has indicated he would be open to forming a government with members of Netanyahu’s Likud party, as well as outgoing Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich’s Religious Zionism, provided their commitment to unity is “sincere”. But a unity government with Netanyahu himself remains unlikely, particularly after Eisenkot denounced his “racist” campaign against Arab parties on Friday. items.title: ‘Obi ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‌⁠​‌‌⁠‌‌​is incorruptible,’ says Kwankwaso
items.description: The vice presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Rabiu Kwankwaso, has described the presidential candidate, Peter Obi, as incorruptible. Kwankwaso made the declaration on Saturday at the 5th convocation ceremony of the Skyline University of Nigeria in Kano. Kwankwaso said the attribute is key and needed in governance of the nation. “One thing I noted in the last few months that we have been working together is that Peter Obi is incorruptible. He’s not somebody that you can go and start thinking of corruption around him, and that is very key in governance in this country,” he said. Kwankwaso pledged that an NDC-led administration would prioritise free education to ensure that no child was denied access to schooling due to financial constraints. “We have so much in common, especially in the issue of education. We believe that together it will be extremely difficult to see how any child will go around in this part of the country or elsewhere begging for what to eat. “In other words, we are working towards free education to ensure that our children are not denied going to school because the parents cannot afford to pay school fees or other expenses. In his remarks, Obi pledged to revive moribund industries in Kano to stimulate economic activities and create employment opportunities. He described Kano as central to Nigeria’s economic development, saying efforts to rebuild the country’s economy must begin with the state. “If we want to fix the North and Nigeria, we must start from Kano. This town represents the soul of Nigeria,” he said. Obi urged the graduates to embrace entrepreneurship, noting that small businesses play a critical role in employment generation and economic growth. (NAN) The post ‘Obi ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‌⁠​‌‌⁠‌‌​is incorruptible,’ says Kwankwaso appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: FO says Climate Minister Musadik Malik nominated to represent Pakistan at SCO moot in New Delhi
items.description: The Foreign Office (FO) said on Saturday that Climate Change Minister Musadik Malik had been nominated to represent Pakistan at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue in New Delhi from Nov 20-22. In a statement, the FO said the gathering would bring representatives from SCO member states to discuss issues related to civilisational dialogue and cultural understanding. “The government of Pakistan remains committed to promoting dialogue among civilisations and fostering people-to-people contacts within the SCO framework in a spirit of mutual respect,” the statement said. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said on X: “Pakistan who is chairing the SCO Council of Heads of State (CHS) in 2026-27, will participate in SCO Civilisational Dialogue in New Delhi this month.” According to Indian news outlet ANI , 10 SCO members — including Pakistan — have been invited to participate in the inaugural Civilisational Dialogue. It added that the gathering was proposed by New Delhi. In a press briefing on Friday, Indian foreign ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that India has invited several SCO member states to take part in the dialogue, adding that New Delhi looks forward to hosting the gathering. Islamabad has a long history of engagement with the SCO through hosting meetings and chairing bodies within the group. It also holds the permanent chairmanship of an SCO working group on poverty alleviation, which focuses on improving living standards across the region. In October 2024, Islamabad hosted the SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting , which India’s Minister for External Affairs Dr S. Jaishan­kar attended on behalf of his prime minister. Jaishankar’s trip, months before the May 2025 military conflict between the neighbours escalated tensions, marked the first such visit by an Indian foreign minister in nearly a decade. Last month, India sent its SCO National Coordinator Alok Dimri to Islamabad for a preparatory meeting for the next SCO CHS meeting in August 2027 , which Pakistan is set to host . “This is my first time on Pakistani soil; these SCO-related programmes will continue throughout the year and culminate in the Islamabad summit,” the Indian official had told PTV News . Pakistan’s chairmanship of SCO CHS marks another step in the country’s growing engagement with the regional organisation, which has expanded its focus from security cooperation to economic development and regional connectivity. DPM Dar has noted that Pakistan’s membership has evolved from observer status to proactive full membership since 2017, reflecting its commitment to multilateralism and regional cooperation. Earlier this month, Pakistan also assumed the chairmanship of the SCO Interbank Consortium (SCO-IBC) for 2026-27, the Ministry of Finance said, with HBL Chairman Sultan Ai Allana taking charge for the period. “The development coincides with Pakistan’s chairmanship of the SCO for the same period, reflecting the country’s role in promoting regional trade, investment, financial connectivity and economic cooperation”, the ministry said. Pakistan also chairs SCO’s Reg­ional Anti-Terrorist Structure (SCO-RATS), a role it assumed in September 2025.

items.title: UKAG : 3 672 étudiants célébrés lors de la sortie de la 25e promotion
items.description: L’Université Kofi Annan de Guinée (UKAG) a célébré, ce samedi 14 novembre, la sortie officielle de sa 25e promotion, à l’occasion d’une cérémonie de remise de diplômes organisée dans l’enceinte de l’institution. Au total, 3 672 étudiants issus des différentes Facultés et Écoles de l’université ont été consacrés, en présence de plusieurs personnalités, dont les Ministre de l’Économie, des Finances et du Budget, Mariama Ciré Sylla, marraine de la promotion, de la Modernisation de l’Administration et de Fonction Publique, François Bourouno, homonyme de la promotion. C'est un moment de fierté, d’émotion et de reconnaissance pour des milliers d'étudiants qui viennent de franchir une étape importante de leur parcours académique. La cérémonie de remise des diplômes de la 25e promotion de l’Université Kofi Annan de Guinée a réuni, responsables universitaires, autorités, familles et proches des récipiendaires. Prenant la parole au nom des majors de cette promotion, Élisabeth Goumou a exprimé sa reconnaissance au président-fondateur de l’UKAG, Dr Ousmane Kaba, ainsi qu’aux responsables administratifs et pédagogiques de l’établissement, pour leur contribution à la formation des étudiants. Elle a notamment rappelé les efforts consentis durant ces années d'études, soulignant que les parcours, qui ont duré entre trois et six ans selon les étudiants, ont été marqués par des défis et des sacrifices. Pour la représentante des majors, l'obtention du diplôme ne doit cependant pas être considérée comme une finalité, mais plutôt comme le début d'une nouvelle étape, celle de la vie professionnelle. « Notre diplôme est une reconnaissance de nos efforts, mais il est surtout une responsabilité : celle de faire bon usage de nos connaissances, de servir avec compétence et intégrité, et de contribuer, chacun à son niveau, au développement de notre société », a-t-elle déclaré, invitant ses camarades à faire preuve de courage, de discipline et de persévérance. De son côté, le Recteur de l’UKAG, le Pr Mohamed Tayeb Laskri a souligné la fierté de l’UKAG de mettre des étudiants compétitifs sur le marché de l’emploi. « Grâce à vous, l’Université Kofi Annan de Guinée est fière de mettre sur le marché de l’emploi des diplômés hautement compétitifs, armés pour relever le défi de notre temps. Nous avons la ferme conviction que vous saurez porter bien haut le flambeau de l’UCAG partout en Guinée, dans la sous-région et au-delà de notre cher continent l’Afrique. Le monde de demain vous tend les bras. Soyez audacieux, intègres, innovants, et demeurez dignes ambassadeurs des valeurs de l’Université Kofi Annan de Guinée », aa-t-il dit. Marraine de cette 25e promotion, la Ministre de l’Économie, des Finances et du Budget, Mariama Ciré Sylla, a, pour sa part, partagé quatre enseignements tirés de son expérience personnelle et professionnelle, en mettant particulièrement l'accent sur la nécessité pour chaque diplômé de définir sa raison d'être, ses ambitions et ses objectifs. Évoquant les perspectives de développement de la Guinée à travers le programme Simandou 2040, elle a estimé que les nouveaux diplômés arrivent sur le marché du travail à un moment particulièrement important pour le pays. « Votre génération a un rendez-vous avec l’histoire, l’histoire de la Guinée. Vous quittez l’université à un moment exceptionnel pour la Guinée. Sous l’impulsion de l’excellence de Monsieur le Président de la République, nous avons aujourd’hui le programme Simandou 2040, qui fixe une ambition de développement durable de notre pays. La Guinée est l’un des pays qui a le plus fort taux de croissance dans la région et dans le monde. On a une opportunité unique de transformer notre pays en un pays qui crée des emplois pour ses jeunes, un pays où les opportunités ne dépendent plus du lieu de naissance, mais plutôt du travail. Une porte vers de nouvelles compétences, de nouvelles opportunités pour vous. Mais une porte ne suffit pas, il faut que vous ayez le courage de la franchir, et c’est là que vous intervenez. Le capital humain, c’est vous. La Guinée a besoin de vous, de votre talent, pas seulement à Conakry, mais aussi dans les régions et dans les préfectures », a-t-elle souligné. La Ministre a également invité les récipiendaires à ne pas attendre d'occuper de hautes fonctions pour contribuer au développement de leurs communautés. Elle leur a notamment lancé le défi de réaliser, au cours des douze prochains mois, au moins une action concrète au service de leur environnement : accompagner une entreprise, créer une activité, former un jeune ou contribuer à résoudre un problème local. S'adressant particulièrement aux majors, elle a rappelé que l'excellence constitue aussi une responsabilité, celle de tirer les autres vers le haut. Aux jeunes femmes diplômées, Mariama Ciré Sylla a recommandé de ne pas limiter leurs ambitions et de cultiver la solidarité pour favoriser leur réussite collective. De son côté, Mohamed Diaby, représentant du parrain de la promotion, l'entrepreneur Bakary Diaby, a insisté sur la nécessité de transformer les connaissances universitaires en compétences et en réalisations concrètes. Il a réaffirmé la disponibilité de Bakary Diaby, le PDG de SOGUIBEC à accompagner les initiatives favorisant l'insertion professionnelle, l'entrepreneuriat et l'épanouissement de la jeunesse guinéenne. Dans la même dynamique, François Bourouno, le Ministre de la Modernisation de l’Administration et de la Fonction Publique et homonyme de cette 25e promotion, a exhorté les nouveaux diplômés à prendre pleinement leurs responsabilités dans la conquête du marché de l’emploi. Pour lui, le diplôme doit être considéré comme un engagement envers soi-même et envers la nation. Il a notamment encouragé les jeunes à ne pas se limiter à la recherche d'un emploi salarié, mais à explorer également les possibilités offertes par l'entrepreneuriat et l'auto-emploi. « Ces opportunités ne vous rejoindront jamais à la maison, ni dans vos espaces du quartier. Ces opportunités, il faut aller à leur recherche. Il faut aller conquérir ces opportunités », a-t-il conseillé, soulignant que les différents projets et réformes engagés dans le cadre du programme Simandou 2040 représentent des perspectives à saisir pour les jeunes compétences. Dans son intervention, le président-fondateur de l'Université Kofi Annan de Guinée, Dr Ousmane Kaba, a dévoilé les statistiques de cette 25e promotion, qui compte exactement 3 672 diplômés issus des différentes facultés et écoles de l'établissement. Ces étudiants proviennent notamment des Facultés des Lettres et Sciences Humaines, Sciences Économiques et de Gestion, Sciences Juridiques et Politiques, Sciences Médicales et Paramédicales, des Sciences Informatiques, de l’Ecole Polytechnique des Ingénieurs, de l’Institut Professionnel et Universitaire, de l’Advanced School and Business Administration. Créée en 1999, l'Université Kofi Annan de Guinée revendique son statut de première et plus ancienne université privée du pays. Selon son fondateur, l'établissement a déjà formé plus de 50 000 diplômés en 25 ans d'existence. Autre particularité mise en avant par Dr Ousmane Kaba : le caractère international de l'institution. « L’Université Koffi Annan de Guinée compte 34 nationalités différentes, venus notamment de plusieurs pays africains, mais aussi de France, des États-Unis, des Pays-Bas, de Thaïlande et de Papouasie-Nouvelle-Guinée ». Visiblement ému au moment de voir partir cette nouvelle génération, le président-fondateur a exprimé sa fierté envers les diplômés, tout en leur souhaitant plein succès pour la suite de leur parcours. Il a également rappelé que certains poursuivront leurs études au sein de l'université en master, d'autres à l'étranger, tandis qu'une partie fera ses premiers pas dans le monde professionnel en Guinée. Un nouveau Un nouveau chapitre s’ouvre désormais pour ces 3 672 récipiendaires appelés à mettre leurs compétences au service de leur avenir et du développement de la Guinée. items.title: Fonds de dotation en sursis (Par Maguette NDONG)
items.description: Les maires et présidents de conseil départemental sont avertis : les Fonds de dotation pourraient être distribués avec un grand retard. C’est Moussa Bala Fofana lui-même qui l’a dit, estimant que le blocage du budget de l’État par les députés de la majorité parlementaire pourrait bel et bien avoir des conséquences sur les fonds que l’État alloue, chaque année, aux collectivités territoriales. Le gouvernement et les députés trouveront-ils une solution d’ici là, rien n’est moins sûr. Mais il faut reconnaître que la plupart de nos communes et départements intègrent ces fonds (dotation, Fect, Cel, ristournes, fonds minier, etc.) dans l’élaboration de leur budget. Jusque-là, les débats étaient axés sur le relèvement du taux des transferts de l'État de 5 à 10 voire 15% du Pib, comme c'est le cas dans plusieurs pays.Dans ce sens, le gouvernement a fait des efforts ces dernières années, en décidant d'injecter 5 milliards de FCfa de plus chaque année sur l'enveloppe des transferts. Par exemple, l’enveloppe globale du fonds est passée de 74,6 milliards de FCfa en 2024 à 79,6 milliards de FCfa en 2025. Aujourd’hui, si ces fonds n’arrivaient pas à temps, la plupart de nos maires et présidents de conseil départemental se trouveraient dans une posture peu enviable. Car où trouveraient-ils des moyens pour faire face aux innombrables charges ? Nous le savons tous, au Sénégal, les élus locaux (maires et présidents de conseil départemental) sont toujours sollicités par les plus démunis pour financer la scolarité de leurs enfants, pour prendre en charge leurs frais médicaux ainsi que d'autres urgences inhérentes aux vicissitudes de la vie. Sans compter les fameux secours auxquels ils doivent faire face pendant les fêtes religieuses comme la Tabaski, Korité, Noël ou encore lors des fêtes de Pâques. Un maire, c'est avant tout le principal acteur social de sa communauté. Celui qui apporte soutien, réconfort et assurance en volant au secours des familles pauvres. Les empêcher d’empocher les fonds de dotation ou retarder la mise à disposition de ces ressources financières, c'est presque les mettre en mal avec leurs administrés. Cette situation inédite à l'Assemblée nationale se passe à un moment où la réflexion est menée sur notre décentralisation. Si la réforme de nos territoires a traversé bien des péripéties, passant de la création des quatre communes à la communalisation universelle, avec l'Acte 3, un nouveau chapitre est ouvert aujourd'hui. Celui de l'Acte 4 qui ambitionne de rendre plus proches les services de l'État aux citoyens, et de créer huit pôles territoriaux. Seulement, la viabilité de certaines communes est aussi une préoccupation de nos gouvernants. Car, avec la communalisation universelle, beaucoup de communes ne parviennent pas à vivre sans l'apport de l'État. Elles manquent de ressources et ne disposent guère de partenariat pouvant booster leur développement. Les temps sont durs donc pour la plupart de nos municipalités, et rares sont les perspectives qui s'offrent à elles pour sortir de ce marasme économique. L'annonce du ministre Moussa Balla Fofana arrive à un moment où la plupart de nos communes se penchent sur leur débats d'orientation budgétaire. Un processus clé dans l'élaboration du budget permettant aux populations et aux élus de cibler les priorités à prendre en charge dans le prochain budget. Aujourd'hui ce débat est parasité par cette déclaration du ministre de tutelle. C'est dire que même lorsque les budgets seront votés et approuvés par les préfets et sous-préfets, tout dépendra de la situation qui prévaut à l'Assemblée nationale. C'est dire que les collectivités territoriales sénégalaises, tout comme bien des secteurs du pays, souhaitent un dénouement rapide voire un dégel entre l'exécutif et le législatif. maguette.ndong@lesoleil.sn

items.title: Experts urge Ghanaian youth to rethink their online behaviour as digital risks grow
items.description: The Society of Private Medical and Dental Practitioners has called for responsible use of social media among young people, warning that growing exposure to online risks could have serious consequences for their mental health and well-being. The society said that although the internet and social media offer opportunities for learning, communication, business and personal development, their misuse exposes young people to cyberbullying, online grooming, sextortion and other harmful activities. The concerns were raised at the society’s maiden public lecture, held at the British Council on Friday, November 13, under the theme, “Growing Up Online: Social Media, Mental Health, and the Future of Ghana’s Youth”. The event brought together members of the society, speakers and students from the African University of Communication and Business (AUCB) and the University of Ghana Medical Students’ Association (UGMSA), among others, to discuss the impact of digital technology on young people. In his welcome address, the National President of the society, Dr Andre Kwasi Kumah, said the decision to organise the public lecture was to expand the organisation’s engagement beyond medical issues to include social developments affecting the population. He explained that although the society had been in existence since 1968, its activities had largely centred on health matters, particularly during its annual general meetings. “Though we’ve been in existence since 1968, we usually have our annual general meetings in the first week of August, and we try to focus on health issues since we are doctors in private practice,” he said. Dr Kumah said the executive had decided to use the public lecture platform to raise awareness about emerging social issues, including the growing influence of social media on young people. He acknowledged the benefits of social media, particularly its ability to connect people, provide learning opportunities and expose young people to new businesses and ideas. However, he said society was concerned about its negative effects, including cyberbullying, low self-esteem and mental health challenges. He said the lecture was intended to encourage an open discussion on how society could maximise the benefits of social media while reducing the risks associated with its use. A Child Protection Specialist with UNICEF Ghana, Hilda Mensah, warned that young people faced several dangers online, including grooming, cyberbullying and sextortion, which could have serious effects on their mental health. In an interview with Myjoyonline, she said the internet had become an important part of everyday life, providing opportunities for people to connect, learn, conduct business and develop new skills. However, she cautioned that these benefits came with risks that required greater awareness and responsible behaviour. “Some of the risks are online grooming, cyberbullying, sextortion, and they have a way of affecting our mental health as young people,” she said. She explained that the consequences could include depression, suicidal attempts, social isolation, strained relationships and a loss of trust in others. Ms Mensah therefore urged young people to be more careful about their online activities and avoid using digital platforms to bully, insult or humiliate others. She encouraged them to use the internet for learning, innovation, personal development and activities that contribute positively to their communities. “What it means is that you use the internet for your own development, innovation, learning, connecting positively, and making, importantly, a contribution to building your society, your community, your family and yourself,” she said. She also reminded young people that their online activities could affect their future opportunities, as information posted on social media could remain accessible long after it was shared. “The internet never forgets,” she cautioned. According to her, young people should think carefully before posting anything online and ask themselves whether their content is useful, educational or contributes to building a better society. “If it does not, pause and refrain from doing so,” she advised. President of the Internet Society of Ghana, Dr Maud Adjeley Ashong Elliot, also urged the public to develop responsible online habits, saying the growing use of digital platforms had made online etiquette as important as conduct in everyday life. She said the internet had become an unavoidable part of modern society and that both young and older people needed to understand how to use it safely. “The internet has come to stay, whether we like it or not. We have to make sure we adapt, and then we survive,” she said. Dr Ashong Elliot warned that unlike some face-to-face interactions, online activities could leave permanent records, making it difficult for users to erase inappropriate content once it had been shared. She said people should think carefully before posting, commenting on, or forwarding information because even deleted content could have been downloaded or saved by others. She also cautioned against the assumption that end-to-end encryption on messaging platforms guaranteed complete privacy. “Most of us are hiding behind end-to-end encryption. It’s a wall, and walls break,” she said. The Internet Society of Ghana president further raised concerns about excessive phone use, saying it could affect productivity, concentration and sleep, even among adults. Sharing her personal experience, she said she had introduced a schedule to limit how frequently she checked her WhatsApp messages after realising how much time she was spending on her phone. She advised users to set boundaries around their online activities, avoid making their phones the last thing they engage with before sleeping, and take regular breaks from digital platforms. Dr Ashong Elliot also called on parents to take a more active interest in their children’s online activities, warning that children could be exposed to harmful content at any time. She said parental supervision should extend beyond what children do outside the home to include their activities on platforms such as YouTube and online gaming services. She encouraged parents to occasionally check the content their children watched and the games they played, stressing that online exposure could happen around the clock. She further urged parents and other adults to avoid forwarding inappropriate videos, even when their intention was simply to inform family members or warn others. She explained that sharing such material could further expose victims to humiliation and violate their dignity. “Digital citizenship” was another key issue she highlighted, saying responsible internet use required users to consider the safety and rights of other people. According to her, people should not share intimate images, harmful videos or other sensitive content involving others, regardless of how widely such material had circulated. Dr Ashong Elliot also urged internet users to develop stronger digital literacy skills to help them identify misinformation, fake news, online scams and phishing attempts. She said people should verify information before sharing it and question suspicious requests for personal information, including their dates of birth and other sensitive details. She advised users to establish why their personal information was being collected and how it would be used before agreeing to provide it. On artificial intelligence, she acknowledged its growing importance but called for responsible and ethical use, particularly among students. She said people should take time to understand the applications they use, read their privacy policies, and consider how their personal information might be collected or shared. “Chatting is good, and AI has also come. Please, it has come to stay, whether we like it or not. But what we want to preach is that let’s use it ethically,” she said. She stressed that users should not simply accept the terms and conditions of digital applications without understanding the information they were agreeing to share. The maiden public lecture forms part of the Society of Private Medical and Dental Practitioners’ efforts to broaden public discussions on emerging social issues and their implications for health and wellbeing. The discussions highlighted the need for a shared approach involving young people, parents, schools, technology users and other stakeholders to promote safer online behaviour while making the most of the opportunities offered by digital technology.

items.title: Portugal redesigns No. 7 shirt to honour Ronaldo after retirement
items.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Portugal have announced a redesign of the No. 7 on their national team shirts in tribute to former captain Cristiano Ronaldo following his retirement from international football. The Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) announced the change on Saturday, saying the new design would preserve the legacy of the number associated with the 41-year-old forward. In a statement shared by football transfer expert Fabrizio Romano, the federation said the decision was another way to immortalise the significance of the number and honour Ronaldo’s contribution to Portuguese football. “This is another way to eternalise the meaning of such a special number and honour the legacy it represents for us. “Because there are stories, memories, all the achievements and emotions, which will forever be linked to Cristiano Ronaldo. “From today we will thus have a different number 7 on the sweater, with the same essence and the same pride, reserving the previous one for the eternalisation of the story that will never be forgotten. Thank you, Cristiano!” the statement read. Ronaldo announced his retirement from the Portugal national team on November 5, bringing an end to his 23-year international career. In a message to Portuguese supporters, the forward said it was time to hand back the national team shirt and captain’s armband after enjoying the privilege of representing his country for more than two decades. “For 23 years, I had the privilege and responsibility of wearing it, defending it, and carrying it with me to stadiums all around the world,” he said. Ronaldo finished his international career as Portugal’s record appearance-maker, with 234 caps, and all-time leading scorer, with 146 goals. He also captained the country to its first European Championship title in 2016 and two UEFA Nations League triumphs in 2019 and 2025. The post Portugal redesigns No. 7 shirt to honour Ronaldo after retirement appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Cocaine busts: NPP cautions members against possible drug planting in luggage at airports, seaports
items.description: The New Patriotic Party (NPP) has cautioned its members, supporters and sympathisers travelling through Ghana’s airports and seaports to be vigilant over what it describes as possible attempts to plant illicit drugs in their luggage. In a travel advisory issued on Saturday, November 14, 2026, the party alleged that individuals affiliated with the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) could attempt to implicate innocent NPP members in narcotics-related offences for political reasons. The statement, signed by the party’s National Vice Chairman, Henry Nana Boakye, linked the warning to what it described as the government’s handling of recent cocaine-related cases and drug trafficking incidents involving Ghanaian nationals abroad. It, however, did not provide evidence of any specific plot to plant drugs in the luggage of NPP members or identify anyone allegedly involved in such an operation. The party urged its members travelling through the country’s entry and exit points to take precautions to protect their belongings against possible interference. “NPP Travellers should remain alert to the possibility of unlawful interference with their luggage or attempts by unscrupulous individuals to introduce prohibited substances like cocaine and other illicit drugs into their personal belongings,” the statement said. Among other measures, the party advised travellers to securely lock and wrap their luggage, maintain personal control over their belongings and avoid accepting parcels or unfamiliar items from other people. It also encouraged travellers to remain alert to suspicious handling of their bags and, where possible, video-record their luggage and the packing of their belongings. The advisory further asked members to inspect their luggage before leaving for the airport, before checking in and whenever their bags were returned to their custody. Travellers were also advised to retain their luggage tags and other travel documents, preserve any relevant evidence and report suspicious incidents to airport security or the appropriate authorities. In its concluding caution, the party urged its members to remain alert, protect their belongings and travel responsibly. The advisory comes amid public debate over cocaine-related incidents and the handling of narcotics cases in Ghana.

items.title: 'Check, one two': Technical glitch hits US presser on air travel chaos
items.description: Trump administration officials were left red-faced on Saturday when their public effort to address the massive tech disruption that grounded thousands of US flights was itself hit with embarrassing technical glitches. Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy took the podium and began addressing a much-anticipated and televised press conference a day after a disastrous nationwide ground stop across US airspace — one blamed on ageing technology — when a deep, echoing hum began to emanate from the microphones and speakers. “Check one two, three four, five six seven?” Duffy said into the mic. As cameras rolled, he paused, looked around, and stepped away. “[I] apologise for that,” he said, as technicians scrambled to replace microphones and adjust cables. Duffy soon resumed, but brittle feedback hit the room seconds later and his demeanour shifted, presumably all-too-aware that the symbolism of an on-camera tech meltdown after such a major flight disruption was not going unnoticed. “This is not operational? OK,” said Duffy, appearing deeply irritated. “This is our kind of, uh, day.” Duffy was speaking to reporters with the head of the Federal Aviation Administration, Bryan Bedford, and, ironically, with the FAA’s chief technology officer Rebecca Guy, who he said was doing a press conference with him for the first time. Duffy and Bedford repeatedly pointed to ongoing systemic issues with transitioning from ageing air traffic control technology from the 1970s and 1980s to more modern equipment. As technicians scrambled, US networks carried the awkward pause — lasting an excruciating three minutes — live on the air.

items.title: Yilwatda charges North-Central APC leaders to unite for Tinubu
items.description: The National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, has charged governors, governorship candidates and party leaders across the North-Central region to unite stakeholders and intensify mobilisation for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in the January 16, 2027 presidential election. Yilwatda gave the charge at the APC presidential campaign rally held at Azaria Road Stadium, Jos, Plateau State, where Tinubu’s campaign train received a large turnout of party leaders, supporters and residents. The APC national chairman expressed satisfaction with the turnout and what he described as a renewed spirit of unity among party leaders and supporters in Plateau State. He urged residents to translate the enthusiasm demonstrated at the rally into votes, insisting that the state must deliver a record-breaking victory for Tinubu. Yilwatda declared that political leaders in Plateau State were fully united behind the President, assuring him that the support demonstrated at the rally would be reflected at the ballot box. He also described Tinubu as a promise keeper who had fulfilled his commitments to Plateau State, saying the administration’s performance provided a basis for continued public support. A major highlight of the rally was the presentation of APC flags to the party’s governorship candidates across the North-Central states, in what the party described as a demonstration of its commitment to strengthening its political structures and securing victory at all levels. Speaking further, Yilwatda urged APC governors, governorship candidates and party leaders in the region to set aside personal interests and political differences, unite all stakeholders and work towards a common electoral objective. In Plateau State, he urged party leaders to consolidate the unity already achieved and mobilise support for Tinubu and all APC candidates. In Benue State, he called on the governor and party leaders to harmonise competing interests, bring political stakeholders together and mobilise voters for the party. For Niger State, the APC chairman expressed confidence in the state leadership’s ability to use the party’s flag as a rallying point to unite members and secure victory for Tinubu and other candidates. Similarly, while presenting the party’s flag to its governorship candidate in Nasarawa State, Wadada, Yilwatda urged him and other party leaders to provide purposeful leadership, unite stakeholders and mobilise support for the President. He also called for concerted efforts towards greater prosperity, peace and development in the state. The APC chairman stressed that the North-Central region must approach the 2027 elections with a common purpose, urging party structures, elected officials, candidates and grassroots mobilisers to intensify engagement with voters. He said the enthusiasm witnessed at the Jos rally must be sustained and translated into votes across the region. “Our strength lies in our unity, our strategy is effective mobilisation, and our destination is victory. I therefore charge all our governors, governorship candidates and party leaders across the North Central to unite every stakeholder in their respective states and work together to deliver maximum votes for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. “The Jos rally has demonstrated what we can achieve when we stand together. We must sustain this momentum, take our message to every community and ensure that our commitment to the President is reflected in our votes,” he said. Yilwatda assured party members and supporters that the APC would sustain its mobilisation drive, strengthen its structures and work collectively towards victory for Tinubu and all its candidates in the 2027 general elections. Agriculture saharienne : alerte sur le niveau des nappes à Biskra, le potager de l’Algérie
items.description: L’extension de l’agriculture dans le sud algérien risque d'épuiser les nappes souterraines, met en garde un député de l'Assemblée populaire nationale (APN). Dans une question orale au ministre de l’hydraulique Lounès Bouzegza, le député de Biskra Abderrahmane Noui a signalé une baisse du niveau des nappes du fait de la forte demande générée notamment par le secteur agricole, dans cette région qualifiée de “ panier alimentaire de l’Algérie ”. Pour pallier la faible pluviométrie (150 à 200 millimètres par an), les agriculteurs ont fortement recours aux eaux souterraines. Une baisse de 5 % par an des nappes de Biskra Le problème touche directement la sécurité hydrique du pays, notamment dans le sud et les Hauts-Plateaux, a indiqué le parlementaire qui s’est présenté comme “ chercheur en hydraulique, en hydrologie et dans l’utilisation de l'intelligence artificielle, de la géophysique et la géolocalisation dans le suivi des ressources en eau ”. Une étude qu'il a lui-même effectuée, “ sur la base de 107 opérations géophysiques ”, et “ une comparaison des données anciennes et actuelles des puits ”, a fait ressortir l'existence de “ changements importants du niveau de la nappe notamment dans les régions est et ouest de la wilaya de Biskra ”. La baisse avoisine les 5 % par an dans certaines zones et le cumul est important au fil des dernières décennies, a-t-il ajouté. À Biskra, l’agriculteur est « obligé de forer de 350 m à 500 m de profondeur pour trouver de l’eau », a-t-il indiqué, en mettant en garde : « Si la situation persiste, dans dix ans, il n’y aura plus ni Deglet Nour, ni les tomates et légumes à Biskra ». “Passer à une gestion proactive de l'eau” Abderrahmane Noui a proposé de passer “ d’une gestion ponctuelle de la crise de l’eau à une planification proactive et à l’investissement dans les ressources en eau de surface et souterraines, en s’appuyant sur des études scientifiques et des technologies modernes ”. “ Il s’agit de savoir où il y aura la baisse, dans quelle proportion et comment agir avant d’atteindre la côte d’alerte ”, a-t-il dit. “ C’est le sujet inéluctable de l’heure. L'Algérie est sécurisée grâce au dessalement et les réserves de la nappe albienne au sud, mais il faut une rationalisation ”, a reconnu le ministre Lounès Bouzegza dans sa réponse. Lounès Bouzegza : “ À Biskra, il y a une baisse de la nappe de plus de 100 mètres ” Le membre du gouvernement a reconnu qu'il y a une baisse des eaux souterraines à cause du changement climatique et la faiblesse des précipitations. “ Il y a eu une forte demande ces dernières années, à Biskra, il y a une baisse de la nappe de plus de 100 mètres ”, a-t-il révélé. “ Biskra n’est qu'un exemple et il faut des solutions au diapason du développement technologique ”, a ajouté le membre du gouvernement. “ Oui, a acquiescé le ministre, il faut passer à une gestion proactive en utilisant l’intelligence artificielle et les nouvelles technologies en coordination avec les experts et les universités afin de prendre les meilleures décisions ” Des mesures ont d’ores et déjà été prises pour étendre le réseau de surveillance du niveau des eaux souterraines, des débits des cours d'eau et des précipitations, a assuré Lounès Bouzegza. L’article Agriculture saharienne : alerte sur le niveau des nappes à Biskra, le potager de l'Algérie est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Économie sociale et solidaire: Vers la signature d’une convention-cadre entre le Sénégal et l’Espagne
items.description: Dans le cadre du renforcement des relations bilatérales dans le domaine de l’économie sociale et solidaire (Ess), l’Espagne et le Sénégal se projettent dans une perspective de partenariat portant sur la migration circulaire, la finance éthique, l’agriculture et le modèle coopératif, l’économie circulaire et le recyclage. RUFISQUE – Le Sénégal et le Royaume d’Espagne entendent dynamiser davantage leur partenariat en matière d’économie sociale et solidaire. Une délégation espagnole, conduite par la secrétaire d’État à l’Économie sociale et solidaire, Maria Amparo, a été reçue, le jeudi 12 novembre, par le ministre de la Microfinance et de l’Économie sociale et solidaire, Dr Alioune Dione, dans son bureau. Cette visite de travail et d’amitié s’inscrit, selon le ministre, dans la continuité directe de la résolution des Nations unies (A/Res/77/281), portée par le Sénégal, l’Espagne, le Chili et la France, érigeant l’économie sociale et solidaire en pilier du développement durable. Elle fait également suite, souligne-t-il, aux démarches entamées lors des précédentes visites de la ministre espagnole au Sénégal, notamment à l’occasion du Forum africain de l’Économie sociale et solidaire (Fora’Ess 2026), organisé à Dakar, au cours duquel des perspectives clés avaient été dégagées avec le Premier ministre. Le ministre Alioune Dione annonce que les travaux actuellement menés avec la Direction de la coopération espagnole donneront lieu à un mémorandum. « Ce document sera transmis aux services diplomatiques pour établir une convention-cadre bilatérale », annonce-t-il. D’après lui, plusieurs points liés à l’insertion socioprofessionnelle constitueront les enjeux centraux de ce partenariat, notamment la question de la migration circulaire. « Face au contexte préoccupant marqué par l’immigration irrégulière vers l’Espagne, les pouvoirs publics entendent mobiliser l’économie sociale et solidaire », estime-t-il. Sur ce point, Dr Dione demeure persuadé que la mise en place d’un mécanisme de migration circulaire constitue une opportunité durable pour répondre au défi de l’emploi des jeunes. Outre cet aspect, cette coopération portera sur la finance éthique, l’économie circulaire, notamment le recyclage des déchets en collaboration avec le Promoged, et surtout sur le domaine agricole, à travers les coopératives agricoles. Sur ce dernier point, le ministre souhaiterait un transfert d’expérience du modèle espagnol. « Près de 80 % de la production agricole en Espagne est réalisée par des coopératives. Nous avons discuté avec la partie espagnole pour appuyer le ministère dans le cadre de la mise en place de fermes intégrées d’économie de subsistance », a-t-il affirmé. Le ministre a annoncé que l’ensemble de ces axes d’action structurera la nouvelle feuille de route. Mohamed DIÈNE (Correspondant)

items.title: Cybersécurité : le Maroc détecte des failles critiques et renforce la protection des plateformes numériques
items.description: Le Maroc renforce son dispositif de cybersécurité face à la multiplication des menaces numériques. En 2026, les opérations d’évaluation et d’audit menées auprès des institutions publiques et des infrastructures d’importance vitale ont permis d’identifier des vulnérabilités critiques sur 31 applications, tandis que plus de 2.100 menaces de sécurité ont été signalées de manière proactive aux organismes concernés. Ces données ont été dévoilées par Abdellatif Loudiyi, ministre délégué auprès de la cheffe du gouvernement chargé de l’Administration de la Défense nationale, lors d’une réunion de la Commission des affaires étrangères, de la défense nationale, des affaires islamiques et des Marocains résidant à l’étranger à la Chambre des représentants. Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre de la Stratégie nationale de cybersécurité à l’horizon 2030, la Direction générale de la sécurité des systèmes d’information (DGSSI) a engagé de nouvelles études consacrées à la maturité cyber des secteurs bancaire, du transport et de l’énergie. Ces trois secteurs sont considérés comme des secteurs d’importance vitale, en raison notamment de l’interdépendance de leurs infrastructures et des conséquences que pourrait entraîner l’interruption de certains services sur l’ensemble de leurs activités. 31 applications présentent des failles critiques Les opérations d’évaluation et d’audit réalisées en 2026 ont porté sur 72 applications électroniques appartenant à des établissements publics et à des infrastructures d’importance vitale. Elles ont permis de détecter des vulnérabilités critiques dans 31 applications. Parmi les 25 applications ayant fait l’objet d’une analyse du code source, 10 présentaient au moins une faille de sécurité critique au niveau de leur architecture logicielle, selon les données communiquées par le ministre. La DGSSI a également lancé une opération urgente d’évaluation de la sécurité des systèmes d’information accessibles via Internet et traitant d’importants volumes de données. Cette opération a couvert plus de 144 plateformes numériques relevant de 45 organismes et infrastructures d’importance vitale. À l’issue des audits, les organismes concernés ont reçu des recommandations et des mesures correctives. Dans certains cas, celles-ci peuvent aller jusqu’à la suspension temporaire d’un système, le temps de corriger les vulnérabilités détectées et de vérifier l’efficacité des mesures mises en place. 419 signalements d’incidents cyber en neuf mois Sur le volet de la surveillance des menaces, le Centre de veille, de détection et de réponse aux cyberattaques de la DGSSI a enregistré 419 signalements d’incidents cyber potentiels entre janvier et septembre 2026. Parmi eux, 123 incidents ont nécessité une intervention directe des services compétents. Dans 47 cas, les interventions ont notamment donné lieu à des analyses numériques destinées à déterminer la nature des attaques, les indicateurs de compromission ainsi que les méthodes utilisées. Les opérations de balayage technique des adresses IP et des noms de domaine accessibles sur Internet ont, de leur côté, généré 1.070 alertes de sécurité concernant des vulnérabilités potentielles, dont 81 alertes liées à des failles à haut risque. Plus de 2.000 menaces signalées aux organismes concernés Le dispositif national de veille et d’analyse des menaces a également permis d’identifier des tentatives de ciblage et des indicateurs de menace visant des ministères, des établissements publics et des infrastructures d’importance vitale. Au total, 2.154 menaces de sécurité ont été signalées de manière proactive aux organismes concernés afin de leur permettre de prendre les mesures nécessaires et de limiter les éventuelles conséquences sur leurs systèmes d’information. En parallèle, le Centre de veille, de détection et de réponse aux cyberattaques a publié 968 bulletins et notes de sécurité en 2026, dont 373 à caractère critique. Les secteurs vitaux passés au crible La DGSSI a par ailleurs achevé en 2026 les résultats d’une étude lancée l’année précédente pour évaluer le niveau de conformité des infrastructures d’importance vitale aux exigences légales et réglementaires en matière de cybersécurité. Selon Abdellatif Loudiyi, le niveau de conformité demeure globalement supérieur à la moyenne, malgré des écarts entre les différentes institutions. Ces disparités nécessitent, selon lui, la poursuite des efforts visant à corriger les insuffisances et à renforcer le niveau de protection. La DGSSI a ainsi transmis à chaque organisme concerné une synthèse de son évaluation, comprenant son niveau de conformité par rapport aux moyennes sectorielle et nationale ainsi que des recommandations destinées à améliorer la sécurité de ses systèmes d’information. Dans le même temps, 24 opérations d’audit ont été réalisées en 2026 auprès de ministères, établissements publics et organismes à caractère stratégique ou vital, conformément aux prérogatives prévues par la loi n° 05.20 relative à la cybersécurité. Ces audits visent notamment à identifier les faiblesses et insuffisances de sécurité et à définir les mesures correctives nécessaires. Le Maroc entend ainsi poursuivre le renforcement de son dispositif national de cybersécurité, avec une priorité accordée aux infrastructures et services dont une interruption pourrait avoir des répercussions importantes sur le fonctionnement de secteurs essentiels. The post Cybersécurité : le Maroc détecte des failles critiques et renforce la protection des plateformes numériques appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .
