items.title: 34 818 kits scolaires et d’hygiène menstruelle réceptionnés
items.description: Le gouvernement du Sénégal, dans sa volonté de lever progressivement les contraintes qui compromettent l’accès et le maintien des filles à l’école, a réceptionné, hier, un lot de 18.893 kits scolaires et de 15.925 kits d’hygiène menstruelle, dits « kits de dignité ». Ils sont destinés à 11 académies du pays, pour un montant de près de 500 millions de FCfa. RUFISQUE – Dans une synergie d’actions et une démarche coordonnée, le ministre de l’Éducation nationale (Men), Moustapha Guirassy, et sa collègue de la Famille, de l’Action sociale et des Solidarités (Mifass), Marie Angélique Diouf, ont procédé, hier, au lancement de la remise des kits scolaires et d’hygiène. Cette action s’inscrit dans le projet « Maintien des filles à l’école », mis en œuvre au titre du Projet d’autonomisation des femmes et du dividende démographique au Sahel Plus (Swedd+), avec l’appui de la Banque mondiale et du Fonds des Nations unies pour la population (Unfpa). « L’accès à l’éducation ne saurait être considéré comme une simple inscription dans un établissement scolaire, mais suppose également que chaque enfant, fille comme garçon, puisse apprendre dans des conditions dignes, favorables et sécurisées, et poursuivre son parcours scolaire jusqu’à son terme », souligne M. Guirassy. Malgré les progrès enregistrés dans le système éducatif, le ministre reste conscient que de nombreuses filles, particulièrement celles issues des familles les plus vulnérables, demeurent confrontées à des difficultés susceptibles de perturber leur scolarité : « précarité économique, insuffisance de fournitures scolaires, difficultés liées à la gestion de l’hygiène menstruelle, stéréotypes de genre, violences et autres facteurs de vulnérabilité », énumère-t-il. Selon lui, ces obstacles appellent des réponses coordonnées, notamment à travers la mutualisation des efforts avec le Mifass. Sa conviction est claire : « aucune fille ne devrait voir son parcours scolaire compromis en raison de sa situation économique ou de difficultés liées à sa santé et à son hygiène menstruelle ». Une rubrique dédiée à l’achat de kits sanitaires La ministre de la Famille, qui a exercé pendant 16 ans dans le milieu scolaire en qualité de professeure et de directrice des études, s’est montrée particulièrement sensible à ces obstacles pédagogiques. « Beaucoup de filles quittent l’école parce que leurs parents n’ont pas les moyens, en début d’année, de leur acheter les fournitures scolaires », déclare-t-elle. En tant que mère, elle relève que l’autre facteur de vulnérabilité demeure la période des menstruations, notamment en raison de la gêne ressentie, des risques d’infection et du manque de concentration. « La jeune fille qui voit ses règles en pleine classe éprouve même de la gêne à se lever pour sortir. Elle préfère rester assise, mais n’écoute plus et ne suit plus le cours », estime-t-elle. La ministre a tenu à porter un plaidoyer auprès de son collègue de l’Éducation nationale. « Il faut, dans le budget des écoles et dans les dotations accordées, qu’il y ait une rubrique spécifique pour l’achat de kits sanitaires », plaide-t-elle. Elle insiste également sur la nécessité de prévoir, dans les infirmeries scolaires, une réserve de kits sanitaires afin de permettre aux filles de vivre sereinement cette période et de suivre correctement leurs cours. Avec ces lots de 15.925 kits d’hygiène menstruelle et de 18.893 kits scolaires destinés à 11 académies, les deux ministères s’attendent à garantir : un ciblage rigoureux, transparent et équitable, fondé sur des critères objectifs de vulnérabilité ; une traçabilité intégrale du processus de distribution ; un accompagnement par des actions de sensibilisation à la santé menstruelle, menées avec les Ong, les enseignants, les parents et les relais communautaires ; ainsi qu’un suivi et une évaluation de l’impact réel de cette initiative sur le maintien des filles à l’école. Mohamed DIÈNE (Correspondant)

items.title: Godfred Apasinaba Wumbei ‘Yellow Man’ wins NDC Northern Regional chairmanship with 328 votes

items.title: ONDA : hausse de 8,3% du trafic des passagers à l'aéroport de Laâyoune
items.description: L’Office national des aéroports (ONDA), a indiqué que l’aéroport Hassan 1er de Laâyoune a enregistré une hausse de 8,3% du trafic des passagers à fin septembre 2026, par rapport à la même période de 2025. Dans ses statistiques relatives au trafic aérien commercial au titre du mois de septembre 2026, l’Office précise que cette plateforme a ainsi accueilli 246.273 passagers durant les neuf premiers mois de l’année en cours, contre 227.385 voyageurs durant la même période de 2025. Pour le seul mois de septembre, l’aéroport Hassan 1er de Laâyoune a accueilli 26.006 passagers, contre 27.723 voyageurs durant le même mois de 2025, soit une baisse de 6,19%. La répartition du trafic aérien des passagers à l’aéroport de Laâyoune, à fin septembre dernier, fait ressortir 207.378 voyageurs sur les vols nationaux, en hausse de 9,82%, contre 38.895 passagers sur les vols internationaux, en progression de 0,9%. Concernant les mouvements aéroportuaires, cette infrastructure a enregistré une progression de 22,65%, avec 2.518 mouvements à fin septembre 2026, contre 2.053 durant la même période de 2025. À l’échelle nationale, les aéroports du Royaume ont enregistré, à fin septembre 2026, un trafic commercial de 29.330.764 passagers, en hausse de 8,74% par rapport à la même période de 2025, qui avait enregistré 26.972.726 passagers. items.title: Décès de Tasnim Ben Zeneb une étudiante engagée au grand cœur
items.description: Dans un communiqué publié ce samedi 14 novembre 2026, l'Université Centrale a annoncé avec une profonde tristesse le décès de Tasnim Ben Zeneb, étudiante inscrite en deuxième année d'anesthésie-réanimation au sein de son École de Santé. En cette douloureuse circonstance, l'établissement d'enseignement supérieur, à travers l'ensemble de son corps enseignant, de son personnel administratif et de ses étudiants, a adressé ses plus sincères condoléances à la famille de la défunte, à ses proches ainsi qu'à l'ensemble de ses camarades de promotion. De son côté le Rotaract Bardo Aqueduc a rendu un vibrant hommage à la cheffe de sa Commission Communication et Média, Tasnim Ben Zeneb. Ses camarades ont exprimé leur profonde douleur face à la perte d'une jeune femme engagée qui a laissé une empreinte indélébile au sein de la communauté rotaracienne. « Tasnim n’était pas simplement une membre de notre club. Elle faisait partie de notre famille rotaracienne. Par sa présence, son engagement et les moments partagés avec elle, elle a laissé une empreinte dans le cœur de chacune et chacun d’entre nous. Son départ laisse derrière lui une immense peine et un vide que les mots ne sauraient exprimer », lit-on dans le post publié par le Rotaract Bardo. Y. N. items.title: Major among 4 troops martyred, 24 terrorists killed during operations in KP and Balochistan: ISPR
items.description: Four troops, including a major, were martyred while 24 terrorists were killed in multiple intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s North Waziristan, the military’s media wing said on Saturday. In a statement , Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said that since Nov 13, armed forces have been conducting multiple IBOs “around Kolpur, Kardagap and Nushki, including area domination and patrolling of the Quetta-Taftan National Highway (N-40) to keep it secure for local traffic and sustain operations”. On the night of Nov 13/14 in Kolpur, security forces “successfully neutralised eight Indian-sponsored terrorists of Fitna al Hindustan ( FAH ), including a suicide bomber, and recovered a large cache of weapons and ammunition”, ISPR said. The state has designated Balochistan-based terrorist groups as Fitna al-Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan. It added that on Nov 14, FAH terrorists “targeted military vehicles on patrol with armed quadcopters”, resulting in the martyrdom of Major Omer Minhas Nasir, resident of Chakwal district, and Havildar Muhammad Adnan Khan from Kotli Sattian. “This cowardly act has not shaken the resolve of the security forces. The tempo of operations will be maintained and IBOs will continue with the same vigour to secure the local population and eliminate the menace of terrorism,” ISPR affirmed. It added that clearance operations in these areas will continue “until the threat is completely neutralised”. This photo, shared by ISPR on Nov 14, shows ammunition and equipment recovered from terrorists in Balochistan. It further said: “Backed by India and other hostile intelligence agencies, FAH is actively trying to use drones and other technical means, including IEDs (improvised explosive devices), to target innocent civilians and security forces, so as to undermine the efforts of the government and security forces to maintain peace and normalcy in the area.” Accusing India of providing terrorists full financial support and supplying it with the “latest gadgetry”, the ISPR asserted, “The security forces are fully alive to this evolving threat and will deny the terrorists any space, whatever means they employ.” ISPR affirmed that the “relentless counterterrorism campaign under vision ‘ Azm-i- Istehkam ’, as approved by the Federal Apex Committee on the National Action Plan , will continue at full pace”. The military’s media wing warned that security forces and law enforcement agencies “will continue at full pace to wipe out the menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country”. In an earlier statement, ISPR said two soldiers were martyred and 16 terrorists were killed as security forces continued a series of IBOs in North Waziristan. According to the military’s media wing, multiple khwarij locations were engaged in the general areas of Mir Ali, Datta Khel and surrounding areas in North Waziristan. “Following fierce fire exchanges, in last twelve hours, 12 khwarij , including two Afghan nationals belonging to Indian-sponsored Fitna al Khwarij were sent to hell in Ali Khel, while two khwarij each were neutralised in Mir Ali and Datta Khel, thereby causing a significant blow to the khwarijs ’ network operating in the area,” ISPR said. Fitna al Khawarij is a term used by the state for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP). ISPR said that during the operations, 43-year-old Havildar Asmat Ali and 32-year-old Naik Aftab Ali embraced martyrdom. “Weapons and ammunition were also recovered from the killed Indian-sponsored khwarij , who remained actively involved in numerous terrorist activities, including the killing of innocent civilians,” it said. The statement said that sanitisation operations would continue to eliminate “remaining holed-up khwarij from these areas”, adding that the counterterrorism campaign would continue at full pace to wipe out the menace of foreign-sponsored terrorism from the country. ‘Step forward in war against terrorism’ President Asif Ali Zardari, in separate statements , paid tribute to the security forces for their successful operations and expressed condolences over the martyrdom of the troops. He expressed his condolences to the bereaved families of the martyrs, terming the sacrifices by officers and soldiers a “source of pride for the entire nation”. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also appreciated the professional competence, bravery and prompt action of the security forces in the operations, state-run APP reported. He prayed for the martyrs’ ranks and for patience for their families. “The enemy is making nefarious attempts to sabotage regional peace by targeting innocent civilians and security personnel. However, our armed forces are fully capable of thwarting every nefarious design of the enemy,” he was quoted as saying. The premier affirmed that operations “against externally sponsored terrorism will continue with full force until its complete elimination”. “The supreme sacrifices of our brave soldiers further strengthen our national resolve to completely eradicate terrorism,” he said in an earlier statement. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said he was deeply saddened by the martyrdom of “brave military personnel in a drone attack on a military convoy in Kirdgap, Mastung”. Strongly condemning the “cowardly attack”, Dar affirmed that the nation “stands united with our armed forces and resolute in its determination to eliminate terrorism”. In his statement, Balochistan Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti termed the killing of eight terrorists a “significant step forward in the war against terrorism”. In a post on X, he declared that “every attempt to spread unrest in Balochistan and block the path to development will be thwarted”. Paying tribute to the martyred major and havildar, CM Bugti wrote, “The state is committed to completely eradicating terrorism and protecting the lives and property of the people. There will be no compromise on peace and stability in Balochistan.” Rise in terrorism The operations come a day after ISPR said 74 terrorists were killed in IBOs in KP and Balochistan. On Friday, it said 43 terrorists were killed during operations conducted over 48 hours in KP, including 35 in North Waziristan’s Mir Ali and eight in Orakzai district. Another 31 terrorists were killed in Balochistan during an operation launched on Nov 3. Pakistan has seen a surge in terrorism, especially in KP and Balochistan, since the banned TTP ended its ceasefire deal with the government in November 2022, vowing to increase attacks. According to Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies , the country’s security environment continued to show considerable volatility from Oct 30 to Nov 5, 2026, with renewed terrorist activity in parts of KP and the former tribal districts, alongside intensified counterterrorism operations and changing patterns of militant violence. While attacks rose from 8 to 20 in former tribal districts, Balochistan presented a different pattern; it recorded 11 attacks, down from 15 the previous week, although fatalities increased from five to seven. The weekly increase came against the backdrop of a substantial month-on-month reduction in terrorist violence recorded during October . Earlier this month, a soldier was martyred and 17 terrorists were killed in two IBOs conducted in Balochistan’s Kachhi and Kharan districts on Nov 1, ISPR said. Correction: An earlier version of this story said 14 terrorists were killed in North Waziristan. The error is regretted.

items.title: Auditor-General to introduce e-tracking system to monitor implementation of audit recommendations
items.description: Ghana’s Auditor-General, Dr Pamela Graham, has announced plans to introduce an electronic tracking system to monitor the implementation of recommendations contained in the Auditor-General’s reports. The system, known as the e-tracker, is expected to enable the public to monitor how Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs), as well as other public institutions, are addressing financial irregularities and other infractions identified by the Ghana Audit Service. Dr Graham disclosed this during a visit to the Ghana Anti-Corruption Coalition (GACC) and other anti-corruption institutions in Accra as part of efforts to strengthen collaboration in the fight against corruption and promote accountability in the public sector. She said the initiative was aimed at addressing concerns over the limited follow-up actions after the publication of audit reports, stressing that identifying irregularities was not enough without concrete measures to ensure accountability. According to her, although the reports are scrutinised by Parliament through the Public Accounts Committee (PAC), more needs to be done after the committee’s hearings to ensure that the issues identified are properly investigated and resolved. She noted that institutions such as the Internal Audit Agency and other relevant bodies have important roles to play in ensuring that infractions are not repeated. Dr Graham said the e-tracker would provide an opportunity for the public to follow the recommendations made by the Audit Service and assess the extent to which public institutions are implementing them. She added that the system would be given the necessary media attention once it is ready to ensure that citizens are adequately informed about how to access and use it. The Auditor-General also emphasised the importance of collaboration among anti-corruption institutions, civil society organisations and the media, arguing that the Audit Service alone could not ensure that its findings translate into meaningful action. “We are just one voice, but if we get everyone collaborating, reading our reports, bringing out what is essential and sharing it with the public, I think that it’s a very good way to go,” she said. Meanwhile, the Executive Secretary of the Ghana Anti-Corruption Coalition, Mrs Beauty Emefa Narteh, has welcomed the Auditor-General’s engagement with anti-corruption institutions, describing it as a positive signal of her commitment to accountability and institutional collaboration. She said the visit was historic, as it marked the first time an Auditor-General had left the office to engage directly with the Coalition. Mrs Narteh noted that the Ghana Audit Service was a member of the GACC, making the engagement particularly significant in strengthening an existing partnership between the two institutions. She said the Auditor-General’s recognition that the fight against corruption required collective efforts demonstrated a willingness to work with citizens and other stakeholders to strengthen accountability in public institutions. Mrs Narteh, however, called for the engagement to go beyond courtesy visits, urging the Auditor-General’s office to establish structured and periodic meetings with civil society organisations to facilitate information-sharing and identify areas requiring improvement. She also encouraged other public institutions, particularly those whose work directly affects citizens, to open their doors to collaboration, insisting that no institution could effectively deliver on its mandate in isolation.

items.title: Nkrumah secured political freedom; Mahama will deliver economic freedom – Gyakye Quayson
items.description: Deputy Foreign Affairs Minister and Assin North MP James Gyakye Quayson says President John Dramani Mahama has an opportunity to build on Ghana’s political independence by securing economic freedom for its citizens. He believes the President is committed to ensuring that the country’s natural and economic resources benefit the wider population rather than remain concentrated in the hands of a privileged few. Mr Quayson also stressed the need to create opportunities for young people to earn decent incomes and improve their living conditions, arguing that Ghana’s resources should work for the benefit of all citizens. He said political leadership must ultimately be judged by its commitment to the welfare of the majority, insisting that those who fail to prioritise the interests of the people should be held accountable. Speaking in an interview with Channel One TV’s Akwasi Addo during the National Democratic Congress (NDC) regional executive election on Saturday, November 14, the Assin North MP urged Ghanaians to support President Mahama in delivering on his mandate. “Kwame Nkrumah gave us political independence. President Mahama is going to give us economic independence,” he said. Mr Quayson questioned the fairness of a system in which many young people struggled without regular incomes despite the country’s considerable resources. “Look at all of you here. I bet 50% of you don’t have a monthly income or resources. You know, it’s not fair to anybody. The resources in this country belong to all of us,” he said. He maintained that citizens must demand accountability from anyone entrusted with political leadership if their welfare is neglected. “I don’t care who becomes the leader. If you come as a leader and you don’t care about the majority of the population, then they should take you out,” he stated. Mr Quayson said the NDC government recognised the responsibility that came with the mandate given to it by Ghanaians and was determined not to disappoint the electorate. “The mandate that Ghanaians have given to the NDC, led by President John Dramani Mahama, we are not taking it for granted,” he added. He expressed confidence that President Mahama would leave a lasting legacy and called on Ghanaians to support his efforts.

items.title: 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐡𝐨𝐧𝐇𝐨𝐮𝐞𝐭𝐒𝐢𝐝𝐰𝐚𝐲𝐚 : Le doublée pour Romain Nikièma, pari réussi pour la 2ᵉ édition
items.description: La cité de Sya a vibré, le samedi 14 novembre 2026, au rythme de la deuxième édition du Marathon Houet des Éditions Sidwaya. 2 400 passionnés de course à pied ont pris part à cette compétition, co-organisée avec la commune de Bobo-Dioulasso, pour renforcer la proximité entre le quotidien Sidwaya et ses lecteurs. Pour cette deuxième édition, deux parcours distincts étaient au programme : le 10 km, ouvert à l’élite régionale et couru en maillots blancs, et le semi-marathon de 21 km, réservé à l’élite nationale arborant des tuniques vertes. Le top départ est donné à 7 heures par le ministre de la Communication, de la Culture, des Arts et du Tourisme, le Camarade Pingdwendé Gilbert Ouédraogo. Sur la distance reine des 21 km, un duel au sommet s'installe entre Romain Nikièma et Roger Nignan. Les deux hommes mènent la danse, se rendant coup pour coup jusqu’à la hauteur du mur de la RTB à proximité de la ligne d’arrivée. Contraint de marquer un temps d'arrêt de quelques minutes, Roger Nignan laisse du terrain, permettant ainsi à son rival Romain Nikièma de filer en solitaire vers la victoire. Romain Nikièma, adjudant des Eaux et Forêts en service à l’École nationale des Eaux et Forêts, franchit la ligne d'arrivée en tête avec un chrono de 1 heures 12 minutes 49 secondes. Déjà sacré l'année précédente, il bat son propre record et conserve son titre : « Il n’est pas question que quelqu’un vienne me battre sur mon terrain », confiera-t-il fièrement. Roger Nignan s’adjuge la deuxième place en 1 heures 13 minutes 30 secondes. Chez les dames sur les 21 km, la palme revient à Marie Aude Saboué. Originaire de la région des Bankui, cette titulaire d’une licence en socio-anthropologie de l’Université de Dédougou se classe brillamment 37e au général. Sur l’épreuve des 10 km, l’intensité est également au rendez-vous. Abdoul Razak Sawadogo s'impose chez les hommes en bouclant le parcours en 36 minutes et 32 secondes. Du côté des dames, c'est la jeune Laurentine Lougué, âgée de 16 ans, qui s’empare de la première place. À noter également la belle performance du benjamin de la compétition, Akim Mohamed Traoré, élève de 11 ans au lycée Alpha Solidarité de Bobo-Dioulasso, qui a forcé l'admiration de tous. Au-delà des performances, la satisfaction était de mise du côté des organisateurs. La Directrice générale des Éditions Sidwaya, Assétou Badoh/Guiré, n'a pas caché sa joie face à l'engouement populaire. « Nous avons pratiquement doublé l’effectif de l’année dernière, avec plus de 2 400 inscrits pour cette édition. Je peux donc dire que nos objectifs sont pleinement atteints. Aujourd’hui, nos regards sont tournés vers l’édition 2027, que nous souhaitons encore plus grande, au profit de la jeunesse burkinabè », s’est-elle réjouie, tout en saluant l'implication précieuse des partenaires, des sponsors et de l'ensemble des participants. Patron de cette deuxième édition, le ministre de la Communication, de la Culture, des Arts et du Tourisme, Pingdwendé Gilbert Ouédraogo, a rappelé succinctement les nombreuses initiatives lancées par le Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, avant d'adresser un message fort à la jeunesse, les invitant à incarner les valeurs d'intégrité et de progrès : « La jeunesse, c’est le fer de lance, c’est l’avenir de notre nation. Pour que cette révolution aille jusqu’à son aboutissement, elle doit être incarnée par cette jeunesse, une jeunesse révolutionnaire. Nous, les jeunes, devons nous engager derrière le camarade Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré ». Le ministre a en outre salué la qualité des récompenses aux meilleurs athlètes, invitant les partenaires, les sponsors et l'ensemble des acteurs à veiller à maintenir, voire à bonifier ces récompenses lors des prochaines éditions. L’édition 2026 était placée sous la présidence de la Camarade Annick Pikbougoum/Zingué Ouattara, Ministre des Sports, de la Jeunesse et de l'Emploi ; le parrainage sportif d’Hugues Fabrice Zango, médaillé olympique ; le coparrainage de la Camarade Ida Ouédraogo/Paré, Directrice générale du Fonds d’appui au sport et à la presse privée Wassa Bondo. Crédit photos : Issa Compaoré et Abdoul Nachire Ussen Sawadogo (images de drone) #Sidwaya.info Les récompenses aux lauréats Pour couronner les efforts des athlètes, le comité d'organisation a récompensé les 40 meilleurs athlètes des différentes catégories. Il s’agit entre autres : • Semi-marathon (21 km – Hommes) : o 1er : Romain Nikièma (26 ans) : Une moto, une enveloppe financière de 300 000 F CFA, des gadgets promotionnels et une médaille. • Semi-marathon (21 km – Dames) : o 1ère : Marie Aude Saboué (27 ans) : Un chèque de 75 000 FCFA, une enveloppe de 100 000 FCFA, un réfrigérateur de marque LG et bien d'autres gadgets offerts par les partenaires. • 10 km (Hommes) : o 1er (Abdoul Razack Sawadogo) : Une moto, une enveloppe de 200 000 F CFA, des gadgets et une médaille (remis des mains de la Directrice générale des Éditions Sidwaya, Assétou Badoh/Guiré). • 10 km (Dames) : o 1ère (Laurentine Lougué) : Une moto et des lots de valeur. Retour en images sur quelques récompenses des meilleurs athlètes

items.title: Burkina Faso : Le ministère de la Justice clôture l’édition 2026 des JIPT sur une note de satisfaction à Ziniaré
items.description: Les activités commémoratives conjointes de l’édition 2026 des Journées internationales de la paix et de la tolérance (JIPT) ont pris fin, ce 14 novembre, à Ziniaré, dans la région de Oubri. Portées par le ministère de la Justice, elles avaient débuté le 23 septembre dernier sous le thème : « La contribution de la Révolution progressiste populaire (RPP) à la promotion des valeurs de tolérance et de paix ». Au cours de cette édition des JIPT, les acteurs ont été appelés à se pencher sur les questions de justice sociale, d'équité, de solidarité et de responsabilité collective. Au-delà des concepts, il s'est agi de faire de ces valeurs des actes qui se traduiront dans le quotidien des citoyens. « Nous avons voulu rappeler une vérité fondamentale. La paix n'est pas seulement l'absence de guerre. Elle est une construction collective, quotidienne et permanente », a expliqué Sy Assétou Barry/Traoré, gouverneure de la région du Oubri. Des communautés à la cérémonie de clôture©️Faso7 Dans son discours lu par la gouverneure, le ministre de la Justice, Me Edasso Rodrigue Bayala, a indiqué que la quête de cette paix s'inscrit dans la vision de la Révolution progressiste populaire, qui recommande une refondation digne et souveraine du Burkina Faso. Les JIPT 2026 ont été marquées par plusieurs activités. Du 27 octobre au 2 novembre 2026, il a été organisé huit conférences en milieu scolaire et cinq rencontres d'échange avec les communautés dans les trois provinces de la région de Oubri. Le panel sur le thème de la commémoration a par ailleurs enregistré la participation de 350 personnes. Les conférences ont permis de sensibiliser au moins 2 400 participants, tandis que les rencontres communautaires ont permis d'échanger directement avec plus de 480 personnes. Les émissions radiophoniques animées en langue mooré ont touché environ 200 000 auditeurs. En somme, la gouverneure de la région de Oubri a souligné qu’au moins un million de personnes ont été sensibilisées à travers la presse écrite, l'audiovisuel, la radio et les médias en ligne. La lauréate en catégorie slam©️Faso7 « Au regard des résultats obtenus et de l'engagement suscité par ses activités au sein des populations, le bilan provisoire est un motif de satisfaction. Il nous rappelle toutefois que la paix est un chantier permanent, que cette commémoration ne soit pas une fin en soi, qu'elle soit le point de départ d'engagement concret dans nos foyers, nos quartiers, nos villages, nos classes et nos administrations », a déclaré la gouverneure de la région. En plus de la course cycliste, le ministère de la Justice a primé les lauréats du concours de poésie et de slam dans la région du Oubri. Dix élèves dans chaque catégorie ont été primés sur 75 candidatures. La première en poésie, Bénédicte Eunice Zongo du Lycée municipal Naaba Koulga de Zorgho, a reçu une enveloppe financière de 100 000 FCFA. Audrey Bayamba, du complexe privé Les Merveilles de Ziniaré, a remporté le premier prix de la catégorie slam avec une enveloppe de 100 000 FCFA. Cheick Habib Désiré BAYILI Faso7 L’article Burkina Faso : Le ministère de la Justice clôture l’édition 2026 des JIPT sur une note de satisfaction à Ziniaré est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Abdul Samad’s late strike sends Pakistan into historic SAFF Championship final
items.description: Abdul Samad Arshad struck a sensational late winner to guide Pakistan into their first-ever SAFF Championship final, as Nolberto Solano’s side held off sustained pressure from hosts Bangladesh to secure a dramatic 1-0 semi-final victory at the National Stadium on Saturday. With Bangladesh dominating possession and looking the more likely side to break the deadlock, Samad produced a moment of individual brilliance in the closing stages to silence the home crowd and make history for Pakistan football. The Denmark-based forward collected the ball on the right, skilfully shifted it between his feet to create space before unleashing a powerful left-footed drive that beat goalkeeper Mehedi Hasan Srabon with around five minutes of regulation time remaining. The victory marks another significant milestone in a remarkable year for Pakistan football, with the national side now just one win away from claiming its first regional title. Bangladesh enjoyed around 62-64 per cent possession and looked to make the most of home advantage, but Pakistan remained disciplined and organised defensively, frustrating the hosts while posing a threat on the counter-attack. Despite having considerably less of the ball, the visitors registered more shots and efforts on target. Bangladesh, who had topped Group ‘A’ unbeaten with victories over Bhutan and Sri Lanka, pressed for an equaliser in the closing minutes. Frustrated home supporters even threw a flare onto the pitch, briefly interrupting play, but Pakistan held firm to secure a famous victory. The result also ends a long history of semi-final disappointment for the Shaheens, who had reached the last four on four previous occasions without managing to progress to the final. Solano’s men had reached the semi-finals as Group ‘B’ runners-up after opening their campaign with a 3-2 defeat to India, despite a spirited late fightback, before responding with a convincing 3-0 victory over the Maldives. The arrival of several overseas-based players, including Samad, for the knockout rounds provided a timely boost, with the group-stage fixtures having fallen outside the FIFA international window. Pakistan will now face arch-rivals and defending champions India in Tuesday’s final after the latter defeated Bhutan 2-1 in the other semi-final. Solano’s side will be aiming to cap their historic campaign by overcoming India and securing Pakistan’s first-ever SAFF Championship title.

items.title: Ken Ashigbey accuses politicians of frustrating galamsey enforcement
items.description: The Convenor of the Media Coalition Against Galamsey, Kenneth Ashigbey, has accused politicians of interfering with efforts by local government authorities to tackle illegal mining, alleging that some Metropolitan, Municipal and District Chief Executives (MMDCEs) willing to enforce the law are being pressured to back down. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, November 14, he said such interference was undermining enforcement efforts and allowing illegal mining to persist. He likened the situation to firefighters becoming arsonists, arguing that some individuals entrusted with fighting illegal mining were themselves involved in activities that perpetuated the menace. “This is evidence of what we talk about, where the firefighters are the arsonists. People that we have put in charge to be able to deal with the situation themselves are the people who are involved in it,” he said. Mr Ashigbey said political pressure was sometimes brought to bear on MMDCEs who wanted to take action against illegal mining operators, weakening efforts to enforce regulations at the local level. “Unfortunately, the situation is that you have DCEs and MCEs even wanting to do the right thing, but because of the politicians, you see them bringing pressure to bear on even the DCEs who want to do the right thing,” he stated. Calls for investigations into threats and attacks The coalition convenor also raised concerns about threats against military personnel and attacks associated with illegal mining, questioning how operators continued to act with apparent impunity despite the presence of security agencies. He called for thorough investigations to identify the individuals and interests allegedly supporting criminal activities in mining communities. “I believe that we need to really investigate this. At the back of all of this is this threat that is happening of these people attacking,” he said. Mr Ashigbey further called for a clear distinction between legitimate mining operators and those involved in criminal activities, including violence, intimidation and the movement of ammunition into mining communities. He said responsible miners should be protected, while those using criminal means to sustain illegal operations should be identified and dealt with decisively. Ashigbey backs Catholic bishops’ call for state of emergency Mr Ashigbey urged President John Dramani Mahama to adopt the recommendations of the Catholic Bishops’ Conference on tackling illegal mining, describing their proposals as a comprehensive response to the crisis. “For me, I think the call of the Catholic bishops, if you read that statement, it has all the solutions that are in it,” he said. He particularly endorsed the bishops’ call for a state of emergency in areas severely affected by illegal mining, arguing that the scale of the problem required a more decisive national response. “I think His Excellency the President needs to listen to the voice of the Catholic bishops to say that enough is enough. Let us declare this state of emergency within these particular spaces,” he added.

items.title: Broken record: Quaid’s visit, an RSS cell, and Dawn under attack
items.description: As refugees continued to pour into Pakistan, often surviving unspeakable violence en route, Quaid-i-Azam Mohammad Ali Jinnah, in a true display of leadership, met with the frazzled masses, urging them to keep hope alive. This, along with the busting of an RSS cell in Karachi, and a violent mob attack on Dawn ’s Delhi press, marked some of the prominent stories from Sept 15 to 21, 1947. Soothing words Many among the millions that had crossed over into Pakistan at the time of Independence had literally been through hell. They had witnessed murder, arson and communal frenzy on their way to what was supposed to be the promised land. In such delicate times, leaders are supposed to put aside protocol and mingle with the masses in order to empathise with them. The Quaid did just that, as a news report from the Sept 18 issue shows. Titled ‘Quaid-i-Azam and sister visit camps of refugees’, it details his visits to three refugee camps and a transit centre. “It was a nerve-wrecking hour that the Quaid-i-Azam and his sister [Ms Fatima Jinnah] spent with the unfortunate victims of Sikh and Hindu communal frenzy in Indian states and the East Punjab. Every refugee to whom they talked had harrowing tales of barbarities and wholesale liquidation of Muslim population to narrate.” Yet despite the horrors they had witnessed, the spirits of the men and women who came to Pakistan remained high, as they “raised full-throated shouts of Pakistan Zindabad and Quaid-i-Azam Zindabad to cheer themselves”. It was also a fact that many who had left behind land and wealth in their ancestral towns and villages were reduced to penury after crossing the frontier. “A jagirdar of Alwar State [now in Rajasthan], who once paid a land revenue of Rs12,000 but now was in tatters, related the gruesome murders of the Muslims of the state and how lakhs and lakhs of Mewati Muslims had either to flee for their lives or were butchered. …” Mr Jinnah was clearly overwhelmed by these accounts of sorrow and savagery, but, in his capacity as governor-general of the dominion, told his people not to lose hope. “The Quaid-i-Azam was visibly moved by their tales of misfortune and asked them to bear the troubles well. The Pakistan State, he said, would do all it possibly could to help them.” Today’s rulers could do much to learn from the empathy and leadership qualities the founder and maker of this nation displayed. The Balochistan question Today, Balochistan is wracked by separatist violence and under-development. The sad truth is that over the past many decades, the province has witnessed many insurgencies, with the rulers unable to progressively resolve its issues, and bring permanent peace to Balochistan. At the time of Independence, Baluchistan, as it was then known, was not one singular entity. In fact, it was divided into so-called British Baluchistan, and four princely states. The latter joined Pakistan in 1948. But early on, there were demands for representative rule, and affiliation with Pakistan. Qazi Mohammad Isa, president of the Baluchistan Provincial Muslim League, was in Karachi to apprise the Quaid and Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan of the demand that “Baluchistan should be made a full-fledged province with a Government responsible to its people.” According to Qazi sahib, the people of the province were eager to join Pakistan. “When his attention was drawn to the question whether Quetta will have to be made over to Kalat State [which had not yet joined Pakistan], he said that the question did not arise at all. The Baluchis wanted to remain in Pakistan, and nothing could be done against the wishes of the people.” The Sangh in Sind The Sangh Parivar — as the stable of far-right Hindu organisations in India are known — has made life for Muslims, Christians and other minority communities in that country very difficult. While the ruling BJP is the political arm of the Sangh, its ideological fountainhead is the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS). Once upon a time, the Sangh was active in what is now Pakistan, and in fact, as the Sept 17 edition shows, an RSS cell in Karachi was busted for apparent involvement in terrorist activities. ‘Sevak Sangh plot for revolution in Pakistan’, the headline read, with the subheadings noting that “thirty terrorist leaders arrested: large quantity of explosives confiscated”. The story went on to say that during house-to-house searches, “sufficient documentary and material proof is believed to have fallen into the hands of the authorities to prove the existence of a widespread underground organisation of the Sangh for disruptive work.” Though the authorities were on the trail of the Sangh extremists for some time, “the chance explosion of a bomb in the house of Rai Bahadur Tota Ram in the Shikarpuri Colony, Karachi [which is located not too far from where the Quaid’s mausoleum now stands] on Sept 10, unexpectedly unravelled the machinations of the Sangh organisation.” Though the RSS leaders and cadres eventually left for India, they were soon replaced by extremists ‘of our own’. Dawn under siege It has always been an uphill struggle for the media to speak the truth in Pakistan. But these curbs, attacks and violent episodes are not new; in fact they go back to the time of Partition. As mentioned in the Sept 16 issue, the Dawn Delhi Press came under attack on Sept 14. As Dawn was considered the voice of the Muslim League, and therefore the voice of the subcontinent’s Muslims, it was an easy target for extremists who opposed Pakistan and the Quaid’s grand old party. The news report, quoting the BBC , said that the attack was a “two-hour gun battle of the Dawn press and the military.” The staff at Dawn Delhi sent the following communication to their colleagues in Dawn Karachi: “We have been in the midst of it since Sunday [Sept 10]. Day and night, death and destruction have been peeping round the corner and we have been at the citadel. … Hell was let loose and we were cut off from the world.” From those harrowing days to the present, the struggle to speak the truth continues. With the advantage of hindsight, one has the opportunity to study the historical cycles in a nation’s life. Thanks to this newspaper’s unique, extensive archive of back issues, one can examine the major political, economic and social trends that have shaped Pakistan and the world over the last seven decades and counting. Cliched as it may sound, history repeats itself, and we — as a state and as a polity — largely refuse to learn from it. Through this platform, we will look back at the ‘big’ stories that made it to the front pages of Dawn, as well as significant developments tucked away in the inside pages, from the birth of Pakistan onwards, and try to put them in perspective. We will study the critical issues of the week, starting from Aug 14, 1947 and examine the major themes and issues that made it to the paper.

items.title: Ken Ashigbey urges Mahama to declare a state of emergency in galamsey hotspots
items.description: The Convenor of the Media Coalition Against Galamsey, Kenneth Ashigbey, has urged President John Dramani Mahama to declare a state of emergency in areas severely affected by illegal mining, citing the growing involvement of individuals entrusted with enforcing mining regulations. He said the fight against galamsey was being undermined by people expected to tackle the menace, describing the situation as one in which those tasked with fighting the problem had become part of it. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, November 14, Mr Ashigbey said the alleged involvement of law enforcement and other responsible officials in illegal mining raised serious questions about the effectiveness of the country’s response. “This is evident of what we talk about the problem, where the firefighters are the arsonists. People that we have put in charge to be able to deal with the situation themselves are the people who are involved in it,” he said. He urged President Mahama to heed the Catholic Bishops’ Conference’s recommendations on illegal mining, describing their proposals as a comprehensive response to the crisis. “For me, I think the call of the Catholic bishops, if you read that statement, it has all the solutions that are in it,” he stated. Mr Ashigbey also expressed concern about reported threats and attacks against military personnel, suggesting that the boldness of individuals involved in illegal mining pointed to possible backing from influential interests. He called for a clear distinction between responsible mining operators and those engaged in criminal activities, including violence, intimidation and the circulation of ammunition in mining communities. He maintained that legitimate mining activities should be protected, while those involved in criminal practices must be identified and dealt with decisively. The coalition convenor further alleged that political interference was weakening efforts by some Metropolitan, Municipal and District Chief Executives (MMDCEs) to enforce mining regulations. He said some officials willing to tackle illegal mining were being pressured by politicians, making it difficult for them to discharge their responsibilities. Mr Ashigbey called for thorough investigations into the threats and attacks associated with illegal mining to identify those behind them. He insisted that the scale of the problem required a stronger response than routine enforcement operations and appealed to the President to adopt the Catholic bishops’ recommendation for a state of emergency in affected areas. “I think His Excellency the President needs to listen to the voice of the Catholic bishops to say that enough is enough. Let us declare this state of emergency within these particular spaces,” he added.

items.title: 2027 UTME: JAMB moves to block wrong subject combinations, introduce pre-registration app
items.description: …to deploy tougher biometric checks, allow candidates report faulty questions, rate CBT centr es By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board, JAMB, is set to introduce sweeping technology-driven reforms ahead of the 2027 Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination, UTME, including a pre-registration mobile application, stricter biometric verification and a system that will automatically block candidates from selecting wrong subject combinations. The reforms, which are aimed at reducing registration difficulties, preventing examination malpractice and strengthening the credibility of the admission process, will also give candidates access to vital admission information before making their course and institution choices. JAMB Registrar, Professor Segun Aina, disclosed the plans on Saturday in Abuja, saying the proposed pre-registration application would enable prospective candidates to complete key registration procedures from the comfort of their homes before visiting accredited centres for final registration. Aina spoke after a five-kilometre fitness walk organised for the board’s staff as part of activities to prepare for the 2027 UTME. He explained that the application would allow candidates to retrieve their personal information from the National Identity Management Commission (NIMC), fill in their biodata, and select preferred subjects, courses, and institutions ahead of the actual registration. According to him, the application would also provide candidates with advance academic guidance, including information on the previous year’s entry marks for their preferred courses. The initiative, he said, would help candidates make more realistic academic choices based on their abilities and available admission requirements, rather than making uninformed selections that could jeopardise their chances of securing admission. “There are a lot of innovations that are coming up. Now we are rolling out what we are calling a pre-registration application. “It’s a mobile application that allows you, from the comfort of your own home, to get your details from NIMC, register with your biodata, select your subjects, your courses and your institution. “During that process, we will be giving some advanced advisory that we didn’t use to give before. For instance, when you are trying to select a course, you will see an idea of what the entry marks for that course were in the previous year,” he said. The registrar said the application would significantly reduce the time candidates spend at registration centres, particularly during the capture of their biometric information. Beyond making registration easier, Aina said JAMB was also working on a system that would make it technically impossible for candidates to submit applications containing incorrect subject combinations for their chosen courses. He noted that candidates had, in previous examinations, made subject selections that were incompatible with their preferred courses, sometimes creating avoidable difficulties in their admission pursuits. “We are going to make that technically impossible, which means you cannot progress with your application if the subject combination is wrong. And a lot of other innovations are coming,” he said. On examination security, the JAMB boss said the board would strengthen biometric verification at examination centres to prevent impersonation, malpractice and other irregularities. He explained that although the board had introduced some concessions to reduce the difficulties candidates encounter when correcting their biodata, such flexibility would be matched with stricter identity checks during the examination. “We have given up some ground and made some concessions to reduce trauma for the candidates in terms of being able to change their biodata and things like that. “And in exchange for that, we will be applying enhanced checks at the point of the examination to make sure that we protect the integrity of the system,” Aina stated. In another innovation, candidates sitting for the 2027 UTME will have the opportunity to report examination questions they consider faulty through a dedicated button on the computer-based test platform. Aina said the feature would enable candidates to flag potentially defective examination questions in real time, allowing the board to investigate such complaints and determine whether the questions were properly framed. He, however, cautioned against the assumption that difficult questions were necessarily faulty, stressing that the proposed reporting mechanism would help JAMB obtain evidence-based feedback for assessing the quality of its examination items. The board is also planning to introduce a post-examination rating system that will allow candidates to assess the quality of services provided by their respective Computer-Based Test (CBT) centres. According to the registrar, the feedback mechanism is intended to strengthen accountability among private sector partners operating the centres while helping JAMB maintain high operational standards. He acknowledged the contributions of CBT centre operators to the examination process since the board adopted computer-based testing more than a decade ago, but stressed that continued partnership would go hand in hand with strict monitoring. The proposed rating system, he said, would give candidates a direct channel to evaluate their examination experience and provide the board with information needed to identify centres that fall short of expectations. Aina said the innovations were part of broader efforts to improve candidates’ experience, eliminate avoidable registration errors, strengthen examination security and sustain public confidence in the nation’s tertiary education admission system. The post 2027 UTME: JAMB moves to block wrong subject combinations, introduce pre-registration app appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ken Ashigbey backs independent probe into NAIMOS-Manso Keniago clash
items.description: The Convenor of the Media Coalition Against Illegal Mining, Ing. Kenneth Ashigbey, has backed calls for an independent investigation into the clash between personnel of the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) and residents of Manso Keniago in the Ashanti Region. He says the inquiry must establish what triggered the confrontation, identify the owner of the excavator at the centre of the disagreement and determine why some residents resisted its movement. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, November 14, Ing. Ashigbey said an independent investigation was necessary to establish the facts and ensure that appropriate measures are taken to prevent a recurrence. “I also associate myself very clearly with their call for an independent investigation. That is very important, but it is important as we do that investigation to find out who the owner of this excavator is,” he said. He suggested that the ownership of the equipment could be an important part of the inquiry, particularly amid questions about whether influential individuals in the community had an interest in preventing its removal. Ing. Ashigbey also urged investigators to examine physical evidence at the scene, including marks left on the ground, to reconstruct the sequence of events. He questioned whether the NAIMOS team was indeed attempting to move the excavator onto a low-bed trailer when residents intervened. “Is it true that excavator belongs to some influential people in the community, and it is the fact that they did not want the excavator moved? Is that what started all of this?” he asked. The incident occurred on November 11, when a NAIMOS task force was transporting excavators seized during an anti-illegal mining operation to a designated location for safekeeping. The confrontation reportedly followed disagreements over the route being used to transport the equipment, with some residents and traditional authorities objecting to the decision to move the excavators through the community along a tarred road. The situation escalated when an armed group reportedly resisted the movement of the machinery, prompting NAIMOS personnel to fire warning shots. The Secretariat said the shots were intended to disperse the crowd and prevent further escalation. Although he called for a thorough investigation, Ing. Ashigbey said he did not support the loss of life in the confrontation. “I don’t associate myself with death or killing of anybody in this,” he said. However, he warned that the growing tendency for residents to threaten officials and security personnel involved in anti-illegal mining operations posed a serious risk to the country’s efforts to combat illegal mining. He described the officers as the country’s last line of defence against the activities of illegal miners and cautioned that attacks on them could encourage similar incidents elsewhere. “But there’s one thing that is happening that is drawing us very close to carnage. It is this tendency for people to threaten the NAIMOS officials and security operators who go to do these things. And you see, this is our very last line of defence,” he said. He warned that allowing such confrontations to continue could embolden others to resist anti-illegal mining operations. “If we lose that line of defence, that last line of defence, what you are going to see is a lot of copycats of these things happening,” he added. Ing. Ashigbey said establishing the circumstances surrounding the Manso Keniago incident was therefore critical to ensuring accountability and introducing measures to prevent similar confrontations. He also welcomed indications that NAIMOS was considering using body cameras to document its operations, describing the move as a step toward improving transparency and accountability. However, he argued that drone footage should also be used during confrontations and not restricted to enforcement activities. He said aerial recordings could provide evidence to help investigators establish what happened when officers encountered resistance during operations. Ing. Ashigbey said proper documentation of such incidents would protect both enforcement personnel and the public and ensure any misconduct could be investigated. Six people have died, whereas two NAIMOS officers who were injured have been treated and discharged. Meanwhile the Lands and Natural Resources Ministry says it has commenced an investigation into the matter.

items.title: President Zardari, PM Shehbaz discuss country's political, economic and security situation
items.description: President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday discussed the country’s political, economic and security situation in detail, the premier’s office said. PM Shehbaz warmly welcomed the president upon his arrival at the former’s residence in Lahore’s Model Town, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) and the Presidency said in identical statements. The premier briefed the president on his recent visit to Turkiye, where he participated in the 31st Conference of Parties to highlight Pakistan’s efforts in climate action. Both leaders exchanged views on “cooperation among allied parties, continuation of consultation and progress on public welfare projects”, the statement said. It added that the two leaders also reaffirmed their commitment to working together to accelerate economic stability and development in the country. National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq Khan, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar, PM’s Adviser on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah, ex-PM Raja Pervez Ashraf, Senator Saleem Mandviwalla and MNA Hamza Shehbaz were also present during the meeting. President Zardari’s meeting with the premier comes just two days after Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi called on the president. After media reports emerged claiming that Naqvi and the president had discussed the possible formation of new provinces during their meeting in Nawabshah, the President House clarified that “no such discussion” took place. The Presidency explained that “matters concerning national security and the regional situation” were discussed during the meeting. The last publicly reported meeting between President Zardari and PM Shehbaz was on Oct 10 , where the two discussed the country’s security situation just a day before the federal government imposed emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. In August, the prime minister had called on the president and briefed him on the Makkah defence pact signed days earlier between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.

items.title: Météo | Tunisie : Les prévisions pour cette nuit
items.description: Selon les prévisions de l'Institut national de la météorologie (INM), le temps sera marqué cette nuit par un ciel partiellement voilé à nuageux sur la quasi-totalité des régions du pays. Les vents souffleront de secteur sud, se montrant faibles à modérés sur la plupart des régions avant de se renforcer progressivement près des côtes nord. En conséquence, la mer sera peu agitée à localement agitée le long du littoral nord, précise l'Institut de la météorologie dans son bulletin. Quant aux températures nocturnes, elles oscilleront généralement entre 15 et 20 °C sur l'ensemble du territoire, et avoisineront les 12 °C sur les régions montagneuses de l'ouest. Y. N. items.title: Coopération Sénégal-Suisse : Bassirou Diomaye Faye veut renforcer les partenariats
items.description: En marge du 20e Sommet de la Francophonie, le président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, a reçu en audience, samedi 14 novembre 2026 à Phnom Penh, le vice-président de la Confédération suisse et chef du Département fédéral des affaires étrangères, Ignazio Cassis. Les échanges ont porté sur les perspectives de renforcement de la coopération bilatérale, notamment dans la formation professionnelle, la santé, l'économie et la gestion de l'eau. Les deux personnalités ont d'abord salué la qualité des relations entre Dakar et Berne, bâties sur une longue tradition de confiance et des valeurs communes de paix, de dialogue et de respect du droit international. Elles ont ensuite passé en revue les différents axes de leur partenariat, avec la volonté de leur donner un nouvel élan. La formation technique et professionnelle figure parmi les secteurs prioritaires. Le chef de l'État a notamment manifesté son intérêt pour l'expertise suisse, reconnue dans ce domaine, afin de mieux préparer la jeunesse sénégalaise aux métiers porteurs et aux besoins de l'économie. La coopération scientifique et médicale, le développement des échanges économiques et les investissements privés suisses au Sénégal ont également été abordés. La gestion de l'eau ainsi que les questions de paix et de sécurité ont aussi figuré au menu des discussions. Au cours de cette rencontre, Bassirou Diomaye Faye a présenté les réformes engagées par son gouvernement pour offrir aux investisseurs un environnement stable, transparent et prévisible. Il a également réaffirmé l'ambition du Sénégal de renforcer la formation de sa jeunesse et de développer les compétences nécessaires à la transformation de son économie. Cette audience s'inscrit dans la volonté du Sénégal de diversifier ses partenariats et de consolider sa coopération avec des pays disposant d'une expertise dans des secteurs stratégiques. L'objectif affiché est de faire de ces relations un levier de création d’emplois, d'amélioration des services de santé et de développement économique. C.G.D

items.title: État civil : le PUMA veut enrôler 1 000 personnes à Kataba 1
items.description: BIGNONA – La commune de Kataba 1, dans le département de Bignona, porte encore les séquelles du conflit armé en Casamance. À l'époque, des milliers d'habitants avaient fui vers la Gambie, abandonnant derrière eux leurs villages et, pour beaucoup, leurs documents d'état civil. De retour chez eux avec le retour de l'accalmie, ces populations sont confrontées à des difficultés pour établir leur identité. Pour les aider à régulariser leur situation, le Programme d'urgence de modernisation des axes et territoires frontaliers (PUMA) organise, depuis vendredi 13 novembre, des audiences foraines de deux jours dans la commune. L'objectif est d'enrôler 1 000 personnes. « Au total, nous allons enrôler 1 000 personnes », a annoncé Maty Mbaye, cheffe du service de l'administration territoriale et déconcentrée, au premier jour de l'opération. Elle a souligné l'importance des besoins en matière d'état civil dans cette localité frontalière de la Gambie. Le PUMA compte ainsi poursuivre ses interventions dans d'autres communes confrontées aux mêmes difficultés afin de permettre au plus grand nombre d'obtenir les documents nécessaires. En 2023, une étude avait recensé près de 10 000 personnes sans acte d'état civil à Kataba 1. À la suite de quatre audiences foraines organisées par la municipalité, 7 500 personnes avaient été enrôlées. Malgré ces avancées, les besoins restent importants. Pour le maire de Kataba 1, Alassane Diatta, l'absence de documents d'état civil a longtemps constitué un frein à la scolarisation des enfants. « Il y a eu beaucoup d'élèves qui ont abandonné les études à cause de ces problèmes de papiers », a-t-il rappelé. Il a toutefois salué la mesure du ministère de l'Éducation nationale autorisant, ces dernières années, les élèves concernés à se présenter aux examens en attendant la régularisation de leur situation. Au-delà de l'identification des personnes, cette opération vise à faciliter leur accès à l'éducation et aux services sociaux, tout en leur permettant de disposer des documents indispensables à la reconnaissance de leur nationalité. Kadidiatou SONKO (Correspondante)

items.title: Burkina Faso : La Fondation Kanis reçoit deux prix lors de la 5e édition de la Nuit des ONG
items.description: La cérémonie de récompense de la 5e édition de la Nuit des ONG s'est tenue le 13 novembre 2026 dans la Salle des banquets de Ouaga 2000. Cet événement, qui distingue les acteurs humanitaires et les initiatives de développement, a mis à l'honneur la Fondation Kanis, lauréate du prix spécial et du prix d'honneur pour ses actions de solidarité. Créée en 2017 sous l'impulsion d'El Hadj Inoussa Kanazoé, président de la fondation et PDG du groupe Cim Metal, la Fondation Kanis est une organisation non gouvernementale burkinabè. Elle a été distinguée pour son engagement et ses efforts remarquables en faveur des populations à la base, soutenus sur fonds propres. Cheick Abdallah Derra, directeur général de la Fondation Kanis, a exprimé sa grande joie et sa reconnaissance après ces distinctions reçues lors de la cérémonie. Pour lui, ces prix ne constituent pas un aboutissement, mais plutôt un encouragement puissant à redoubler d'efforts. La Fondation Kanis, lauréate du prix spécial du promoteur et du prix d'honneur pour ses actions de solidarité -©Faso7 ​ Selon ses explications, l'action de la fondation vise à soutenir les populations vulnérables afin d'appuyer l'État dans sa mission sociale. À cet effet, l'organisation prévoit d'intensifier ses interventions en s'étendant au-delà des grands centres urbains, comme Ouagadougou, pour agir au plus près des réalités du terrain. « Le patron El Hadj Inoussa Kanazoé faisait beaucoup d'œuvres sociales. Mais quand il a vu le grand nombre de déplacés, d'enfants, de femmes, de veuves et d'orphelins, il s'est dit : pourquoi ne pas créer une fondation qui apportera réellement de l'aide à la population, afin de soulager aussi la souffrance de l'État ? C'est pour cette raison que nous avons posé beaucoup d'actes sanitaires, installé des châteaux d'eau, offert de nombreux forages et réalisé plusieurs établissements, surtout au profit des déplacés, pour alléger leurs souffrances », a-t-il déclaré. La Fondation Kanis reçoit deux distinctions lors de la 5e Nuit des ONG -©Faso7 Depuis sa création, la fondation s'est illustrée dans le domaine éducatif par la construction et la réhabilitation d'infrastructures scolaires, l'attribution de bourses et l'appui à l'excellence académique. Elle s'est également investie dans les secteurs sanitaire et social à travers le soutien aux centres de santé, l'accès à la médecine spécialisée et l'assistance aux personnes déplacées internes (PDI). Ces distinctions récompensent en outre ses distributions de vivres et son accompagnement à l'insertion socio-économique des jeunes. D'après le directeur général, ces initiatives contribuent durablement au bien-être des communautés. Elles permettent de réduire les inégalités par des réalisations concrètes, telles que les infrastructures hospitalières, plutôt que par de simples effets d'annonce. La Fondation Kanis distinguée pour son engagement et ses efforts remarquables en faveur des populations à la base, soutenues grâce à ses propres moyens -©Faso7 ​ Cheick Abdallah Derra a réaffirmé la volonté de l'organisation d'élargir son champ d'action hors de la capitale pour répondre aux besoins vitaux des populations, ainsi qu'à ceux des familles des Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS) tombées sur le champ d’honneur. « Nous allons faire beaucoup plus que ce que les gens pensent. Parce que, quand tu descends sur le terrain, tu vois la réalité : si tu as quelque chose à manger, tu prends vraiment conscience de la nécessité de partager » , a-t-il indiqué. Cet événement met ainsi en lumière les efforts continus de l'organisation pour soutenir les couches sociales les plus fragiles du Burkina Faso. items.title: Samson’s Take: Ghana’s media madness – Politicians created it
items.description: Sam Nartey George says Ghana’s broadcasting landscape is overcrowded, describing the proliferation of radio and television stations as pure madness. He’s absolutely right about the problem. But who created this madness? Who distributed broadcasting frequencies like political souvenirs? And who frustrated attempts to bring sanity to the industry? Politicians without principles. The NDC and the NPP alike. Check the insane saturation: in 2017, this small country of ours had 471 authorised FM stations. Nigeria, big brother Nigeria, with over 170 million people at the time. Even some said it was about 200 million. Six times more than our population had fewer. They had 361. Kenya had 118. And again, big South Africa had only 59 FM stations. By 2023, Ghana had added nearly 300 more to the 471 stations. We had a staggering 747 FM authorisations. Today, according to the NCA’s June 2026 figures, we have 793 authorised FM stations. Yes, only 571 are operational, though. Add 170 television authorisations, and you have almost a thousand. That’s 963 radio and television stations in a small country of approximately 35 million people. Is this media pluralism or an industry drowning in political patronage, commercial desperation, and professional indiscipline? Media freedom is a constitutional treasure, but multiplying stations does not necessarily multiply quality journalism. I have personally fought this battle. I was counselled, challenging the reduction of FM transmission coverage from 100 kilometres to 45 kilometres. When Nana Akufo took over, petitions for some sanity to Minister Ursula Owusu-Ekuful and the President went unheeded. The policy created room for more frequency allocations in an already overcrowded, saturated market. The plain plan was this, very obvious. The NDC had distributed frequencies like confetti to cronies, and the NPP needed to outdo them in the race to the bottom. It is the usual senseless partisan conduct, disguised as national interest. Politicians, politically exposed persons, and their associates have acquired broadcasting frequencies frequently during their party’s reign. Some obtained authorisations without the resources to operate viable stations, treating frequencies as commodities for eventual transfer. Some sold them. The public airwaves became instruments of private political advantage. You recall the crackdown under Ursula Owusu-Ekuful in 2017? 131 FM stations or authorisation holders were sanctioned. By October 2019, 57 stations had reportedly been closed down. Radio Gold and Radio XYZ became prominent casualties of the enforcement controversy. And who fiercely challenged those closures? Even the closures included the genuinely defaulting operators who needed correction and sanction. Sam Nartey George. Yes, he challenged that. Today, he is a minister threatening to shut down politically and religiously affiliated broadcasters. I welcome his recognition of the problem. But where is the consistency? What was objectionable under Ursula cannot suddenly become acceptable under Sam George, simply because political power has changed hands. Regulation must be lawful, fair, and independent of party interest. Now consider the broadcasting bill. For nearly two decades, Ghana has failed to enact comprehensive broadcasting legislation. Earlier drafts sought to prohibit political and certain religious ownership, restrict multiple frequencies, and expose beneficial owners. Those restrictions threatened powerful political and commercial interests. And that was central to the prolonged resistance and inaction. We still haven’t passed it. Indeed, the 2024 draft relaxed earlier ownership prohibitions. The politicians expected to legislate against media concentration were themselves beneficiaries of the system. And now social media has multiplied the problem. That’s what it has done. Facebook, TikTok, YouTube, and other platforms have opened extraordinary opportunities for free expression and citizen participation. But alongside the benefits is an epidemic of misinformation. Yes, I mean that. An epidemic of misinformation, fabricated stories, character assassination, hate speech, dangerous health claims. Some people are doing juju and multiplying money on TV. Kids have had to kill and murder their own because they were misled on these platforms. And deliberate political disinformation is going on. Reputations are destroyed for clicks. Falsehoods are monetised. Ethnic and religious tensions are inflamed. Public confidence in democratic institutions is undermined. I repeat that. Public confidence in democratic institutions is undermined. It’s become very difficult to rule or to govern a small country like ours. Some political actors finance, encourage, and amplify these abuses only to complain when the same weapons are turned against them. That is political hypocrisy. Freedom of expression is not freedom from irresponsibility. Neither is it permission to endanger public health, destroy reputations, or poison democratic governance. But the solution cannot be arbitrary closures, censorship, or ministerial control of public discourse. Pass a constitutionally sound broadcasting bill. Disclose the real owners of stations. Restrict excessive ownership concentration. End speculative frequency trading. Enforce lawful conditions without political discrimination. Empower the independent National Media Commission. Stop appointing politicians to that place. Strengthen professional accountability and confront online harms through lawful proportionate measures. Sam George has correctly diagnosed a long-standing national problem. We check it now, or it will destroy this country. Now let him prove that his principles apply equally to NDC and NPP interests because the airwaves belong to Ghanaians, not politicians, party financiers, or even media moguls. Ghana needs more responsible journalism, not merely more broadcasting stations. Mr GJA President, these are really not jobs, as you complain that people’s jobs are at stake. How much are they paid at these stations, these mushrooming FM stations? How much are the people paid? You see why it is so easy for them to be turned into political tools: more truth, not more noise. More public service, not political propaganda. The politicians helped create this mess. Let them now demonstrate the courage and principles to clean it up, beginning with their own interests, and that is my take.

items.title: Microsoft announces service 'restored', global outage over
items.description: Tech giant Microsoft said on Saturday it has “restored service” to customers, effectively drawing a close to a massive outage that caused chaos and disrupted public services and business around the world. “We have completed our efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions,” the US-based company said in an X post. Microsoft had already reported a “broad recovery” for Outlook email and other services the day before, stating the major disruption was due to a technical issue and “not related to cyber or AI/agents”. The outage swept the globe on Thursday, taking the company’s products offline in at least 74 countries and territories across the Americas, Europe, Asia and Africa, according to the monitoring site Downdetector. Microsoft had attributed the disruption to “elevated load” on its infrastructure. It said the stoppage affected its Outlook email service, as well as Microsoft’s Teams communication platform and the company’s Copilot AI assistant. Microsoft on Friday apologised for the global outage as it reported a “broad recovery” for Outlook email and other services. The company ruled out any malicious “cyber or AI” activity as the cause of the outage, which affected several Microsoft products and disrupted health care services, delayed corporate earnings reports and left schools struggling to communicate. “We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners,” Microsoft said on X, adding that full services were still being restored after the outage started on Thursday.

items.title: Musk says Nvidia will lose 'critical' deals without Jensen Huang
items.description: Elon Musk said on Saturday that chipmaker Nvidia would lose “critical” deals without its now-ousted chief executive officer (CEO) Jensen Huang. Huang stepped down on Thursday after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy, plunging the chipmaker into crisis and sending shockwaves across an AI industry he helped bankroll. In a post on X, Musk said that while Huang drove the supply chain “brilliantly” at Nvidia, many such deals were “a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract”. “Without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost.” The SpaceX boss went on to praise the former Nvidia CEO: “If Jensen gave me his word about compute delivery or I asked for components to be accelerated, he always came through. “Sure, we’d put together a purchase order at some point later, but I never for a second thought it wouldn’t happen.” The billionaire has separately said on X that a petition was underway to reinstate Huang and that he would sign it. It was not immediately clear whether Musk was referring to the internal effort reported by Wired . Nvidia declined to comment on the Wired report as well as Musk’s post. Reuters could not independently verify the reports. Pressure had mounted on Huang after reports said the 63-year-old, who is married, had an affair with Alice Huang , an unrelated former executive of Singapore-based company Megaspeed, who US authorities had been investigating. Nvidia then said its board was probing whether its then-CEO “has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort”. On Thursday, CNN reported that the US intelligence community was still working to understand the relationship between Alice Huang and the Chinese government, with multiple sources telling CNN that the intelligence collected on her to date does not prove that she was acting as a spy for Beijing. The report said there was “disagreement among US officials about the strength of the evidence that Alice Huang was recruited by the Chinese Ministry of State Security (MSS)” to spy on Jensen Huang. Insiders and tech titans in the running Huang’s exit plunges the $4 trillion company into uncertainty and threatens to disrupt an AI ecosystem that he helped bankroll by pouring Nvidia’s swelling cash pile back into cloud providers, suppliers and the industry’s biggest labs. Nvidia’s board has approached British chipmaker Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas in its search for a potential successor to Jensen Huang, the Financial Times reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter. Haas’s name has been making the rounds among analysts since Huang’s exit. He spent seven formative years at Nvidia, rising to vice president and general manager of its computing products business, before joining Arm in 2013. Nvidia’s finance chief Colette Kress is currently interim CEO. Nvidia’s board said it was in the process of selecting a search firm for the CEO role and had not formally engaged any potential candidates. Some analysts expect the next CEO to break from Huang’s three-decade reign as the hands-on “chief conductor” who personally steered engineering roadmaps, geopolitical negotiations over exports to China and massive investments across the AI ecosystem. A potential shift toward a more institutional leadership structure would come as Nvidia faces heightened regulatory scrutiny and a growing consensus among US lawmakers to further restrict the company’s chip exports to China. Analysts view Kress as a steady financial authority, while veteran engineer Ian Buck is seen as a top candidate after leading development of CUDA, the software platform that powers Nvidia’s AI chips. Apart from Haas, external names discussed by analysts include AMD chief Lisa Su, who has navigated the key China market, and Micron chief Sanjay Mehrotra, whose memory chips power Nvidia servers. Other candidates cited by industry watchers include Marvell head Matt Murphy and Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji, who oversaw the iPhone maker’s in-house silicon development. Former Apple chief Tim Cook was floated by US President Donald Trump, as Nvidia’s board evaluates whether to prioritise financial continuity, deep technical expertise, or experience running a global tech heavyweight.
